# Phase C3: system nodes build their own cores - implementation plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or
> superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for
> tracking.

**Goal:** A system node's settings name everything its core is built from: its ROM and its battery or savestate seeds
as **resources**, typed byte blocks TS puts into the engine, and every construct-time field as a plain setting. The node
builds its core at activation through a new `rp.host.systems/1`. `buildCore` and the parked cores go, the settings blob
and its three decoders go, and a construct-time edit resets the system at once carrying its battery, instead of waiting
for the user to press Reset.

**Architecture:** Per [docs/modular-graph-phase-c3-design.md](modular-graph-phase-c3-design.md). Two RPCs join the
emulator facet: `putResource` (bytes, a path native reads, or the embedded ROM) and `releaseResource`, both over the
engine's existing `ResourceTable`. A node holds a resource its settings name through `rp::resource_ref<Type>`, a
settings field type that pins at create, drops at destroy, and makes a moved `res:N` ref a rebuild that `node.hpp`
decides itself, so a system node keeps `stateless_prepare`. A node that names a `system` builds its core at activation
through `rp.host.systems/1` from a typed config (`SameBoyConfig`, `MesenNesConfig`, `MesenSmsConfig`, `MesenGbaConfig`),
claims the snapshot slot, and fills the plan's `SystemTable` entry before the plan is published; `destroy` releases both
at reclaim. TS owns resources per system (`graph/systemResources.ts`: counted handles, a ROM retained only when its
source is the same), `buildGraph` names them, every store verb puts them and publishes, and `setRoleConfig` runs the
construct-time edit as a rebuild under a new id. Then the old path is deleted and its callers move to documents
built from resources.

**Tech stack:** C++20 with Catch2 (`retroplug-graph-test`, `retroplug-engine-graph-test`) and reflect-cpp, the graph
layer of Phases A to C2, TypeScript on txiki (`pnpm test` mock tier, `pnpm test:native` real host).

**Where this plan departs from the design.** The design as committed (2c0e22c6) was written before the prototype; the
plan follows what was built, and Task 5's docs commit lands the design with its Status line, its section 9 questions
answered and a section 10, "Found while building". In short:
- **Resources reach a node as a settings field, not as a planner binding.** `rp::resource_ref<Type>` pins what it
  names at create and drops it at destroy, `node.hpp` puts the handle in every settings object the node is handed,
  and a moved ref is a rebuild `node.hpp` decides by comparing the refs a prepared settings object names with the
  pins its instance holds. So `rebuild_key` covers `system`, `romName` and the construct-time fields only; a
  resource ref in it would be harmless, and is not needed. A plan's own binding pin could not serve: the executor
  binds a port view only just before `process`, `prepare` or `step`, which is after the planner created and
  activated the node, and the core is built at activation.
- **The build is a host interface of its own, `rp.host.systems/1` with `build` and `destroy`.** It is not an
  extension of `rp.host.cores/1`, whose shapes differ and which stays exactly as it was for the old path until Task
  4. The engine owns the one `SystemFactory`; the plan's `SystemTable` entry for a built system is filled as its
  node activates, so the table is complete before publication, and the table's pre-fill from the engine's live cores
  is what shows a node reused from the previous plan (which returns from `activate` without building). The snapshot
  slot is claimed after the build, because the claim seeds the slot from the core and a GBA should pay its boot
  before a full pool refuses it; a build outside the `setGraph` that activates it is refused.
- **A node seeds its applied state from what its build applied**, less what the typed config does not carry (a Game
  Boy's serial-out capture), so its first application finds every value equal and calls nothing, as C2's nodes do.
- **ROM reuse is decided by the source, not the verb.** A rebuild shares its ROM resource only when the source is
  the same (the same path, the same embedded marker, or the same image byte for byte), so a rebuild after an asset
  role folded in a different image puts its own; `reload` always puts a fresh one, because the ROM watcher's reread
  is one of its callers. The design's table says `reload` keeps "the same ROM"; the identity still holds, the
  resource does not.
- **A stored value the role schema would have repaired now leaves the node's default.** There is no blob to carry a
  clamped or rounded value, so `systemKnobs` leaves out a value the node would refuse and notes it, and the node's
  own default applies. An unknown label keeps its meaning, because the schema's default and the native default
  agree.
- **A construct-time edit is compared through the role schema's parse** of the stored config (falling back to the
  raw config where that parse throws). Without that, a sparse stored config looked like it moved every omitted field
  to its default, so a live knob edit rebuilt the system under a new id.
- **The SDK contract changes, and code written against the old one keeps working.** A construct-time `setRoleConfig`
  rebuilds the system under a new id, carrying its battery; `systems()` exposes the live list. Code written against
  the previous contract followed such an edit with `reset(id)`: the store remembers which id a rebuild replaced, so
  a `reset` of that id resets its replacement, following a chain to the live system and answering its new id. Both
  consumer suites use that pattern unchanged (BlipToaster's `bootRomWith`, NESVJ's `bootRegion`), and both pass
  against the prototype (57 and 19 test files). `sdk-types.d.ts` says both: the new contract and the compatibility
  path.
- **The construct-time test does not cover every field.** The design's section 7 asked test:native to show every
  construct-time field landing with no Reset, the SD root among them; `app-construct-edit` covers the NES FIFO
  profile, the export mode and SMS FM, and the final design's section 7 records that as what C3 pins.
- **The SMS / Game Gear staged stem defaults per system.** A node that sends no `romName` stages under
  `system-<id>`, unique within a Project, so two unnamed systems never share a battery; only a real stem lets two
  instances of one game share its own. TS always sends the stem, `mgb` for the embedded ROM.
- **Task 4 deletes the old path and moves its test callers.** Gone: `buildCore`, `BackendConstructSpec`,
  `RpcBuiltCore`, `toBuildSpec`, the parked cores (`parkCore`, `takeCore`, the re-park of a core a refused document
  took, the free of what stayed parked, re-rating them), `SystemBuildSpec`'s blob with its three role-config
  decoders, `rp.host.cores/1`, the RPC service's second `SystemFactory`, `SameBoyConfig::linkGroupId`, and the
  `core` field and its `unknown-core` / `core-type` refusals. Twelve cases were old-path-only (seven in
  `EngineGraph.test.cpp`, three in `SystemNode.test.cpp`, one in `ScriptPacks.test.cpp` and one in
  `NesSplitRouting.test.cpp`); the table below names each one's counterpart. Eleven of the twelve are in the
  engine-graph binary; one of those, "buildCore and setGraph over the RPC layer", is rewritten in place as its
  counterpart, so the binary loses ten cases: 201 -> 191 (193 with the review's two new cases). NesSplitRouting's
  case is in `retroplug-audio-test`, which goes 102 -> 101. One property, the gain's first-value snap, has no
  counterpart on the old path's terms, because a node's core is always freshly built and the block the gain first
  lands in is silent: a different staging pins it (a savestate seed taken mid-chime), and a `SystemTable` pre-fill
  case is added in the same commit. A NES tap record can still match a fresh core allocated where the armed one was
  freed; the hazard predates C3, and TS's monotonic system ids keep it unreachable.
- **`ConstructSpec` stays**, as TS's description of what to boot rather than a wire type; its `core` field selects
  no core and names the kind of core whose role config `coreConfig` is.

### Task 1: resources over RPC, and a node that names one in its settings

Design section 4. A resource is an immutable byte block with one owner and a pin per holder, already in the graph
layer's `ResourceTable` but reachable from nothing: no RPC makes one and no node reads one. This task adds the two RPCs
(`putResource` with bytes, a path native reads, or the embedded ROM's marker; `releaseResource`, the owner's
idempotent drop), the host interface a node reaches them by (`rp.host.resources/1`), and the settings field type
`rp::resource_ref<Type>` that pins what it names at create, drops it at destroy, and makes a moved ref a rebuild
`node.hpp` decides. A toy node and a toy pair of nodes pin the contract: the cases here are the resource layer's, not a
system node's.

**Files:**
- Create: `packages/native/test/graph/Resources.test.cpp`
- Modify: `packages/native/cmake/tests.cmake`, `packages/native/src/graph/GraphHost.cpp`, `packages/native/src/graph/GraphHost.hpp`, `packages/native/src/graph/ResourceTable.hpp`, `packages/native/src/graph/node.hpp`, `packages/native/src/graph/rp_node.h`, `packages/native/src/host/engine/Engine.cpp`, `packages/native/src/host/engine/Engine.hpp`, `packages/native/src/host/rpc/BackendRpcRegistration.hpp`, `packages/native/src/host/rpc/BackendTypes.hpp`, `packages/native/src/host/rpc/EngineRpcService.cpp`, `packages/native/src/host/rpc/EngineRpcService.hpp`, `packages/native/test/engine-graph/EngineGraph.test.cpp`, `packages/native/test/graph/GraphRig.hpp`, `packages/retroplug/src/backend.ts`, `packages/retroplug/src/realBackend.ts`, `packages/retroplug/test/meta.test.ts`, `packages/retroplug/testing/mockBackend.ts`, `spec/02-native-host.md`

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests**

`Resources.test.cpp` (new) in `retroplug-graph-test`: `rp.test.resource` acquires its `rom` at create (an absent field
leaves it unheld) and releases it at destroy, a moved ref rebuilds with the old pin dropped and the new one taken, a
knob edit keeps the pin and the instance, a create whose second resource field is missing pins nothing of the first,
and a refused plan unwinds every pin the plan's new instances took; plus the engine's own table seen through the RPC
from `EngineGraph.test.cpp` (bytes, a path, the embedded `mgb` marker, all four refusals, the idempotent drop, ids
never reused). `GraphRig` gains an optional extra package for the toy types, and `tests.cmake` registers the new
source in `retroplug-graph-test` and gives the engine-graph binary the `.sav` path its seed cases read:

Create `packages/native/test/graph/Resources.test.cpp`:

````cpp
// A node that reads a resource its SETTINGS name (docs/modular-graph-phase-c3-design.md section 4, and section 2.5 of
// the main design for the lifetime rule): the authoring layer pins it at create through rp.host.resources/1 and drops
// the pin when the instance is destroyed, a ref that moves rebuilds the node, and a document naming a missing, dropped
// or wrong-typed resource is refused with the field's name in the reason. Driven on a quiescent GraphHost except where
// a case keeps the audio side owning the drain, which is how a pin is watched across a reclaim.
#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include <string>

#include "GraphRig.hpp"
#include "graph/node.hpp"

using namespace rp::graph;
using namespace rp::graph::test;

namespace {

// The toy: its one resource field is a rom, `model` stands in for a construct-time field that only a rebuild changes,
// and `level` is a knob a commit applies to the instance it has, so a case can see the instance's pin reach the
// settings object a commit installs.
struct ResourceNodeSettings {
    rp::resource_ref<"rom"> rom;
    std::uint32_t           model = 0;  // the rebuild key
    double                  level = 1.0;
};

struct ResourceNode {
    static constexpr const char* id = "rp.test.resource";
    using Settings = ResourceNodeSettings;
    struct { rp::audio_out<rp::mono> out; } outputs;

    // A keyed type whose prepare is stateless, as a system node is: a new `model` rebuilds, while `level` alone does
    // not, and the prepare reads only what create fixed (the key and the resource pins).
    static std::uint32_t rebuild_key(const Settings& s) { return s.model; }
    static constexpr bool stateless_prepare = true;

    const Settings* settings = nullptr;
    bool            sawBytes = false;  // the settings object on_settings last saw carried a handle
    std::uint32_t   bytes = 0;         // and the payload was this many bytes
    std::string     ref;               // the ref it named
    float           level = 0.0f;
    std::uint32_t   blocks = 0;        // state a rebuild loses

    void on_settings(const Settings& s) noexcept {
        settings = &s;
        const rp_bytes* b = s.rom.bytes();
        sawBytes = b != nullptr;
        bytes = b ? static_cast<std::uint32_t>(b->size) : 0;
        ref = s.rom.ref;
        level = static_cast<float>(s.level);
    }
    void process(const rp::Block& b) noexcept {
        for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < b.frames(); ++i) outputs.out[0][i] = level;
        ++blocks;
    }
};

// Two resource fields, so a case can watch a pin that names none keep its place in the settings' field order.
struct PairNodeSettings {
    rp::resource_ref<"rom">  rom;
    rp::resource_ref<"sram"> seed;  // absent in most documents
    double                   level = 1.0;
};

struct PairNode {
    static constexpr const char* id = "rp.test.resources";
    using Settings = PairNodeSettings;
    struct { rp::audio_out<rp::mono> out; } outputs;

    std::uint32_t romBytes = 0;
    std::uint32_t seedBytes = 0;  // 0 when the document names none
    std::uint32_t blocks = 0;     // state a rebuild loses
    void on_settings(const Settings& s) noexcept {
        const rp_bytes* r = s.rom.bytes();
        const rp_bytes* b = s.seed.bytes();
        romBytes = r ? static_cast<std::uint32_t>(r->size) : 0;
        seedBytes = b ? static_cast<std::uint32_t>(b->size) : 0;
    }
    void process(const rp::Block&) noexcept { ++blocks; }
};

const rp_package* resourcePackage() {
    static const rp_node_type* const kTypes[] = {rp::node_type<ResourceNode>(), rp::node_type<PairNode>()};
    static const rp_package kPackage{RP_ABI_VERSION, R"({"id":"rp.test.resource","version":"1.0.0"})", 2, kTypes};
    return &kPackage;
}

// One node, `r`, whose settings name `ref` (a rom); a document of just it, and one that also carries a node whose rom
// names no live resource, which fails its CREATE after `r` has pinned.
std::string doc(const std::string& ref, double level = 1.0, std::uint32_t model = 0) {
    return R"({"nodes":[{"id":"r","type":"rp.test.resource","settings":{"rom":")" + ref + R"(","level":)" +
           std::to_string(level) + R"(,"model":)" + std::to_string(model) + R"(}}],"wires":[]})";
}
std::string docWithRefusedNode(const std::string& ref) {
    return R"({"nodes":[{"id":"r","type":"rp.test.resource","settings":{"rom":")" + ref +
           R"("}},{"id":"bad","type":"rp.test.resource","settings":{"rom":"res:999"}}],"wires":[]})";
}
std::string resRef(ResourceTable::Id id) { return "res:" + std::to_string(id); }

std::string pairDoc(const std::string& rom, const std::string& seed, double level = 1.0) {
    std::string settings = R"({"rom":")" + rom + R"(")";
    if (!seed.empty()) settings += R"(,"seed":")" + seed + R"(")";
    settings += R"(,"level":)" + std::to_string(level) + "}";
    return R"({"nodes":[{"id":"r","type":"rp.test.resources","settings":)" + settings + R"(}],"wires":[]})";
}

struct Rig : GraphRig {
    Rig() : GraphRig(HostConfig{48000.0, 64, Target::Desktop}, 8, resourcePackage()) {}
    ResourceNode& toy() { return node<ResourceNode>("r"); }
    PairNode&     pair() { return node<PairNode>("r"); }
};

}  // namespace

TEST_CASE("a node pins the resource its settings name, and the pin goes when the instance does", "[graph][resource]") {
    Rig rig;
    const auto rom = rig.resources.createBytes("rom", {0x52, 0x50, 0x4f, 0x4d});
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(resRef(rom))).ok);
    CHECK(rig.resources.pinCount(rom) == 1);
    CHECK(rig.toy().sawBytes);
    CHECK(rig.toy().bytes == 4);
    CHECK(rig.toy().ref == resRef(rom));

    rig.run();
    CHECK(rig.toy().blocks == 1);
    CHECK(rig.resources.pinCount(rom) == 1);  // a block neither pins nor drops

    // The document drops the node: quiescent, its plan is reclaimed in the same call, and the pin goes with it.
    REQUIRE(rig.set(R"({"nodes":[],"wires":[]})").ok);
    CHECK(rig.resources.pinCount(rom) == 0);
    CHECK(rig.resources.liveCount() == 1);  // the owner still holds it
}

TEST_CASE("a settings change that keeps the resource keeps the pin, and the new settings object carries the handle",
          "[graph][resource]") {
    Rig rig;
    const auto rom = rig.resources.createBytes("rom", {1, 2, 3});
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(resRef(rom))).ok);
    rig.run();
    rig.run();
    CHECK(rig.toy().blocks == 2);

    // `level` moves, the ref does not: the instance is kept (a swap), and the settings object prepare parsed carries
    // this instance's pin, so the node reads its bytes from the committed settings too.
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(resRef(rom), 0.5)).ok);
    CHECK(rig.resources.pinCount(rom) == 1);
    rig.run();
    CHECK(rig.toy().blocks == 3);  // the same instance
    CHECK(rig.toy().level == 0.5f);
    CHECK(rig.toy().sawBytes);
    CHECK(rig.toy().bytes == 3);
}

TEST_CASE("a resource a node's settings name must be a live resource of the field's type", "[graph][resource]") {
    Rig rig;
    const auto rom = rig.resources.createBytes("rom", {1, 2, 3});
    const auto sram = rig.resources.createBytes("sram", {4, 5});
    const auto gone = rig.resources.createBytes("rom", {6});
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(resRef(rom))).ok);
    REQUIRE(rig.resources.drop(gone));

    const auto refused = [&](const std::string& document) {
        const SetGraphResult r = rig.set(document);
        REQUIRE_FALSE(r.ok);
        REQUIRE(r.errors.size() == 1);
        CHECK(r.errors[0].code == "create-failed");
        return r.errors[0].message;
    };
    const std::string unknown = refused(doc(resRef(999)));
    CHECK(unknown.find("rom:") != std::string::npos);
    CHECK(unknown.find("not a live resource") != std::string::npos);
    const std::string dropped = refused(doc(resRef(gone)));
    CHECK(dropped.find("not a live resource") != std::string::npos);
    const std::string wrongType = refused(doc(resRef(sram)));
    CHECK(wrongType.find("sram resource, not a rom") != std::string::npos);
    const std::string malformed = refused(doc("res:007"));
    CHECK(malformed.find("is not a resource reference") != std::string::npos);

    // Every one of them left the running plan as it was: the node still runs, its own pin untouched.
    CHECK(rig.resources.pinCount(rom) == 1);
    CHECK(rig.host->node("r") != nullptr);
    rig.run();
    CHECK(rig.toy().blocks == 1);
    CHECK(rig.toy().bytes == 3);
}

TEST_CASE("a create that fails on a later resource field drops the fields it already pinned", "[graph][resource]") {
    Rig rig;
    const auto rom = rig.resources.createBytes("rom", {1, 2, 3});
    const auto gone = rig.resources.createBytes("sram", {4});
    REQUIRE(rig.resources.drop(gone));  // its owner is gone, and nothing pins it
    CHECK(rig.resources.liveCount() == 1);

    // The pair node pins `rom` first and is refused on its second field. Reaching that second field at all is what
    // says the first was acquired: a create that could not pin `rom` would have stopped there, naming `rom`.
    for (const std::string& seed : {resRef(gone), resRef(999)}) {
        const SetGraphResult refused = rig.set(pairDoc(resRef(rom), seed));
        REQUIRE_FALSE(refused.ok);
        REQUIRE(refused.errors.size() == 1);
        CHECK(refused.errors[0].code == "create-failed");
        CHECK(refused.errors[0].message.find("seed:") != std::string::npos);
        CHECK(rig.resources.pinCount(rom) == 0);  // `rom`'s pin went with the instance that took it
    }

    // A leaked first pin would keep `rom` resident after its owner lets go.
    CHECK(rig.resources.drop(rom));
    CHECK(rig.resources.liveCount() == 0);
}

TEST_CASE("a change of the named resource rebuilds the node, and the old pin drops at reclaim", "[graph][resource]") {
    Rig rig;
    const auto first = rig.resources.createBytes("rom", {1, 2, 3});
    const auto second = rig.resources.createBytes("rom", {1, 2, 3, 4, 5});
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(resRef(first))).ok);
    rig.run();
    rig.run();
    REQUIRE(rig.toy().blocks == 2);

    // The audio side owns the drain, so the plan that ran the first instance is not reclaimed until it is told to.
    rig.host->setAudioThreadOwns(true);
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(resRef(second))).ok);
    CHECK(rig.resources.pinCount(first) == 1);   // the plan still running it pins it
    CHECK(rig.resources.pinCount(second) == 1);  // and the fresh instance pinned what it names
    rig.host->setAudioThreadOwns(false);         // flush: adopt, then reclaim what the swap replaced
    CHECK(rig.resources.pinCount(first) == 0);
    CHECK(rig.resources.pinCount(second) == 1);

    rig.run();
    CHECK(rig.toy().blocks == 1);  // a fresh instance, its state not carried over
    CHECK(rig.toy().bytes == 5);
    CHECK(rig.toy().ref == resRef(second));
}

TEST_CASE("a keyed stateless node rebuilds on its key, swaps a knob, and rebuilds on a moved ref",
          "[graph][resource]") {
    Rig rig;
    const auto rom = rig.resources.createBytes("rom", {1, 2, 3});
    const auto other = rig.resources.createBytes("rom", {4, 5});
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(resRef(rom), 1.0, 0)).ok);
    rig.run();
    rig.run();
    REQUIRE(rig.toy().blocks == 2);

    // `level` alone: the instance is kept, so its block count continues and its pin never moves.
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(resRef(rom), 0.5, 0)).ok);
    CHECK(rig.resources.pinCount(rom) == 1);
    CHECK(rig.toy().blocks == 2);
    rig.run();
    CHECK(rig.toy().blocks == 3);
    CHECK(rig.toy().level == 0.5f);
    CHECK(rig.toy().sawBytes);

    // The key moves: a fresh instance, whose state starts over, pinning the same resource.
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(resRef(rom), 0.5, 1)).ok);
    CHECK(rig.resources.pinCount(rom) == 1);
    CHECK(rig.toy().blocks == 0);
    rig.run();
    CHECK(rig.toy().blocks == 1);

    // The ref moves with the key unchanged: a rebuild all the same, because node.hpp decides it, not the key.
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(resRef(other), 0.5, 1)).ok);
    CHECK(rig.resources.pinCount(other) == 1);
    CHECK(rig.resources.pinCount(rom) == 0);
    CHECK(rig.toy().blocks == 0);
    rig.run();
    CHECK(rig.toy().blocks == 1);
    CHECK(rig.toy().ref == resRef(other));
    CHECK(rig.toy().bytes == 2);
}

TEST_CASE("a refused plan unwinds the pins its new instances took", "[graph][resource]") {
    Rig rig;
    const auto held = rig.resources.createBytes("rom", {1});
    const auto fresh = rig.resources.createBytes("rom", {2, 2});
    // A plan running `r` on `fresh` first proves a create pins what it names; switching to `held` drops that pin, so
    // the refusal below starts with no pin on `fresh` but its owner still holding it.
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(resRef(fresh))).ok);
    CHECK(rig.resources.pinCount(fresh) == 1);
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(resRef(held))).ok);
    CHECK(rig.resources.pinCount(fresh) == 0);

    const SetGraphResult refused = rig.set(docWithRefusedNode(resRef(fresh)));
    REQUIRE_FALSE(refused.ok);
    // One error, and it names `bad`: `r`'s create succeeded, and only its success puts the pin on `fresh` there.
    REQUIRE(refused.errors.size() == 1);
    CHECK(refused.errors[0].code == "create-failed");
    CHECK(refused.errors[0].nodeId == "bad");
    CHECK(rig.resources.pinCount(fresh) == 0);  // dropped as the refused plan's instances unwound
    CHECK(rig.resources.pinCount(held) == 1);   // the running plan's untouched
    CHECK(rig.host->node("r") != nullptr);
    rig.run();
    CHECK(rig.toy().blocks == 1);
    CHECK(rig.toy().ref == resRef(held));

    // Only pins keep an entry alive after its owner lets go, so a leaked pin would leave it here.
    CHECK(rig.resources.drop(fresh));
    CHECK(rig.resources.liveCount() == 1);  // `held` alone
}

TEST_CASE("a resource the owner drops while a plan pins it stays readable, and is freed after that plan is",
          "[graph][resource]") {
    Rig rig;
    const auto rom = rig.resources.createBytes("rom", {7, 7});
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(resRef(rom))).ok);
    CHECK(rig.resources.drop(rom));        // the owner lets go; the node's pin keeps it alive
    CHECK_FALSE(rig.resources.drop(rom));  // and a duplicate drop cannot take the pin with it
    CHECK(rig.resources.liveCount() == 1);

    rig.run();
    CHECK(rig.toy().sawBytes);
    CHECK(rig.toy().bytes == 2);

    // The instance holding the pin plans on, so a later document naming the same resource does not depend on when the
    // last plan happened to be reclaimed.
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(resRef(rom), 2.0)).ok);
    rig.run();
    CHECK(rig.toy().bytes == 2);
    CHECK(rig.toy().level == 2.0f);

    // The plan that reads it goes, and with the last pin the resource is freed. A document naming it now refuses at
    // create, where a plan after the reclaim would.
    REQUIRE(rig.set(R"({"nodes":[],"wires":[]})").ok);
    CHECK(rig.resources.pinCount(rom) == 0);
    CHECK(rig.resources.liveCount() == 0);
    const SetGraphResult refused = rig.set(doc(resRef(rom)));
    REQUIRE_FALSE(refused.ok);
    CHECK(GraphRig::codes(refused) == "create-failed");
    CHECK(refused.errors[0].message.find("not a live resource") != std::string::npos);
}

TEST_CASE("a node with a resource field that names none keeps its other fields' pins in place", "[graph][resource]") {
    Rig rig;
    const auto rom = rig.resources.createBytes("rom", {1, 2, 3});
    const auto seed = rig.resources.createBytes("sram", {9, 9});
    REQUIRE(rig.set(pairDoc(resRef(rom), "")).ok);
    CHECK(rig.resources.pinCount(rom) == 1);
    CHECK(rig.resources.pinCount(seed) == 0);
    CHECK(rig.pair().romBytes == 3);
    CHECK(rig.pair().seedBytes == 0);
    rig.run();
    rig.run();
    REQUIRE(rig.pair().blocks == 2);

    // A knob alone while the seed is ABSENT keeps the instance: the placeholder hold keeps the pins aligned with the
    // fields, so a rebuild does not start the node over every time an optional seed is not named.
    REQUIRE(rig.set(pairDoc(resRef(rom), "", 0.5)).ok);
    CHECK(rig.resources.pinCount(rom) == 1);
    CHECK(rig.pair().blocks == 2);
    rig.run();
    CHECK(rig.pair().blocks == 3);

    // Naming the second resource moves the refs, so it is a rebuild: the fresh instance pins both.
    REQUIRE(rig.set(pairDoc(resRef(rom), resRef(seed))).ok);
    CHECK(rig.resources.pinCount(rom) == 1);
    CHECK(rig.resources.pinCount(seed) == 1);
    CHECK(rig.pair().romBytes == 3);
    CHECK(rig.pair().seedBytes == 2);
    CHECK(rig.pair().blocks == 0);
    rig.run();
    rig.run();
    REQUIRE(rig.pair().blocks == 2);

    // A setting that is not a resource keeps the instance, and both handles are carried into the new settings object.
    REQUIRE(rig.set(pairDoc(resRef(rom), resRef(seed), 0.25)).ok);
    CHECK(rig.resources.pinCount(rom) == 1);
    CHECK(rig.resources.pinCount(seed) == 1);
    CHECK(rig.pair().seedBytes == 2);
    CHECK(rig.pair().blocks == 2);
    rig.run();
    REQUIRE(rig.pair().blocks == 3);

    // Dropping the seed's ref is a rebuild too: the counter starts over, and the pin goes with the instance.
    REQUIRE(rig.set(pairDoc(resRef(rom), "")).ok);
    CHECK(rig.pair().blocks == 0);
    CHECK(rig.resources.pinCount(seed) == 0);
    CHECK(rig.pair().seedBytes == 0);
    CHECK(rig.pair().romBytes == 3);
}
````

````diff
+
+TEST_CASE("putResource and releaseResource over the RPC layer", "[engine-graph][resource]") {
+    // The two calls createEmulatorClient makes for a resource (docs/modular-graph-phase-c3-design.md section 4): the
+    // answer realBackend turns into {id} or {error}, and the drop. Driven through the QuickJS codec, because the
+    // optional fields are the wire shape: `id` a number when a resource was created, `error` a string when none was.
+    struct Js {
+        JSRuntime* rt  = JS_NewRuntime();
+        JSContext* ctx = JS_NewContext(rt);
+        ~Js() {
+            JS_FreeContext(ctx);
+            JS_FreeRuntime(rt);
+        }
+    } js;  // first, so it outlives the server holding its context
+
+    Engine           e(kRate);
+    SystemFactory    factory;
+    registerCoreBackends(factory);
+    QueuedInvoker    invoker(e);
+    EngineRpcService rpc(e, factory, invoker);
+    rpcpp::QuickJSTransport                                   transport(js.ctx, [](JSContext*, JSValue) {});
+    rpcpp::TypedRpcServer<rpcpp::Empty, rpcpp::QuickJSCodec> server(transport, rpcpp::QuickJSCodec{js.ctx});
+    registerEmulatorRpc(server, rpc);
+
+    // One call, answering its `result` (owned by the caller).
+    const auto call = [&](const char* method, const std::string& params) -> JSValue {
+        const std::string src = std::string("({jsonrpc: '2.0', id: 1, method: '") + method + "', params: [" + params + "]})";
+        JSValue message = JS_Eval(js.ctx, src.c_str(), src.size(), "<rpc>", JS_EVAL_TYPE_GLOBAL);
+        if (JS_IsException(message)) {
+            JS_FreeValue(js.ctx, message);
+            return JS_UNDEFINED;
+        }
+        std::optional<rpcpp::QuickJSOut> reply = server.processMessage(message);
+        JS_FreeValue(js.ctx, message);
+        if (!reply) return JS_UNDEFINED;
+        JSValue answer = reply->materialize(js.ctx);
+        JSValue result = JS_GetPropertyStr(js.ctx, answer, "result");
+        JS_FreeValue(js.ctx, answer);
+        return result;
+    };
+    struct Answer {
+        std::uint32_t id = 0;  // 0: absent
+        std::string   error;   // empty: absent
+    };
+    const auto put = [&](const std::string& params) {
+        Answer a;
+        JSValue result = call("putResource", params);
+        JSValue id = JS_GetPropertyStr(js.ctx, result, "id");
+        if (JS_IsNumber(id)) {
+            double value = 0.0;
+            JS_ToFloat64(js.ctx, &value, id);
+            a.id = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(value);
+        }
+        JS_FreeValue(js.ctx, id);
+        JSValue error = JS_GetPropertyStr(js.ctx, result, "error");
+        if (JS_IsString(error)) {
+            if (const char* text = JS_ToCString(js.ctx, error)) {
+                a.error = text;
+                JS_FreeCString(js.ctx, text);
+            }
+        }
+        JS_FreeValue(js.ctx, error);
+        JS_FreeValue(js.ctx, result);
+        return a;
+    };
+
+    // The bytes themselves: an immutable resource of the type the spec gave, owned and pinned by nobody yet.
+    const Answer byBytes = put("{type: 'rom', bytes: new Uint8Array([1, 2, 3, 4])}");
+    REQUIRE(byBytes.error.empty());
+    CHECK(byBytes.id != 0);
+    const rp_resource* bytesRom = e.resource(byBytes.id);
+    REQUIRE(bytesRom);
+    CHECK(std::string(bytesRom->type) == "rom");
+    const auto* payload = static_cast<const rp_bytes*>(bytesRom->payload);
+    REQUIRE(payload);
+    CHECK(payload->size == 4);
+    CHECK(payload->data[2] == 3);
+    CHECK(e.resourcePinCount(byBytes.id) == 0);
+
+    // A path: native reads the file, so a battery or a 32 MB ROM never crosses the bridge. The SMS tracker's `.sav` is
+    // a real battery the tree already carries.
+    const Answer byPath = put(std::string("{type: 'sram', path: '") + RP_SMS_SAV_PATH + "'}");
+    REQUIRE(byPath.error.empty());
+    const rp_resource* sram = e.resource(byPath.id);
+    REQUIRE(sram);
+    CHECK(std::string(sram->type) == "sram");
+    CHECK(static_cast<const rp_bytes*>(sram->payload)->size == std::filesystem::file_size(RP_SMS_SAV_PATH));
+
+    // An embedded ROM, by its marker.
+    const Answer byMarker = put("{type: 'rom', embedded: 'mgb'}");
+    REQUIRE(byMarker.error.empty());
+    REQUIRE(e.resource(byMarker.id));
+    CHECK(static_cast<const rp_bytes*>(e.resource(byMarker.id)->payload)->size == rp::embeddedMgbRom().size());
+
+    // Every refusal answers `error` and creates nothing: a type no node reads, a file that is not there, a marker the
+    // binary does not carry, and a spec with no source or two.
+    for (const auto& refused : {
+             put("{type: 'kit', bytes: new Uint8Array([1])}"),
+             put("{type: 'sram', path: '/nonexistent/rp-resource.sav'}"),
+             put("{type: 'rom', embedded: 'nope'}"),
+             put("{type: 'rom'}"),
+             put("{type: 'rom', bytes: new Uint8Array([1]), embedded: 'mgb'}"),
+             put("{type: 'rom', bytes: new Uint8Array(0)}"),
+         }) {
+        CHECK(refused.id == 0);
+        CHECK_FALSE(refused.error.empty());
+    }
+    // An empty byte block is a resource for a seed (a blank battery), but never for a rom.
+    const Answer blank = put("{type: 'sram', bytes: new Uint8Array(0)}");
+    REQUIRE(blank.error.empty());
+    CHECK(static_cast<const rp_bytes*>(e.resource(blank.id)->payload)->size == 0);
+    CHECK(put("{type: 'kit', bytes: new Uint8Array([1])}").error.find("\"rom\", \"sram\" or \"state\"") !=
+          std::string::npos);
+    CHECK(e.resource(byBytes.id) != nullptr);  // the refusals left what was there alone
+
+    // The owner's drop: idempotent, answered as a boolean, and the id stays dead.
+    const auto release = [&](std::uint32_t id) {
+        JSValue result = call("releaseResource", std::to_string(id));
+        const bool dropped = JS_IsBool(result) && JS_ToBool(js.ctx, result);
+        JS_FreeValue(js.ctx, result);
+        return dropped;
+    };
+    CHECK(release(byBytes.id));
+    CHECK_FALSE(release(byBytes.id));
+    CHECK(e.resource(byBytes.id) == nullptr);
+    CHECK_FALSE(release(9999));
+    // Something the running plan pins would stay alive here instead; nothing pins these, so a drop frees them.
+    CHECK(release(byMarker.id));
+    const Answer later = put("{type: 'rom', bytes: new Uint8Array([9])}");
+    REQUIRE(later.error.empty());
+    CHECK(later.id > byMarker.id);  // ids are never reused
+}
````

- [ ] **Step 2: Run the tests to see them fail**

Run: `cmake -S . -B build && cmake --build build --target retroplug-graph-test -j$(nproc)`
Expected: FAIL: `retroplug-graph-test` stops at the names this task adds (`rp::resource_ref`, `rp.host.resources/1`); that binary never sees `putResource` / `releaseResource`, which live in `EngineGraph.test.cpp` and are first built by Step 6's `pnpm test:plugin` (the engine-graph binary). With those in place and the node hooks unwired, the toy node's cases fail one by one: a create takes no pin, a moved ref keeps the instance, and over the RPC a put answers no id.

- [ ] **Step 3: Acquire a resource from a settings field**

`rp_node.h` gets the interface and its name; `GraphHost` answers it over the engine's `resources_`, with reasons
phrased to finish the node's own sentence; `ResourceTable.hpp`'s header now names both pin kinds (a plan's binding and
a node's settings held by its instance). `node.hpp` gets `rp::resource_ref<Type>`, a top-level settings field that
reflect-cpp reads and writes as the string `"res:N"` and that keeps the resolved `const rp_resource*`, and the
`acquireResources` / `resolveResources` steps wired into create, prepare and destroy: an instance holds its pins and
releases them after its own destructor; a prepare that keeps the same refs copies the instance's pins into the new
settings object, so a knob edit never re-pins; and a prepare whose refs moved asks for a rebuild even when the type's
key says nothing moved. The pin is owned by the instance, not the settings object:

````diff
 }
 
+const rp_resource* GraphHost::resourceAcquire(void* ctx, std::uint32_t id, const char* type, rp_error* err) {
+    auto* self = static_cast<GraphHost*>(ctx);
+    rp_resource* r = self->resources_.get(id);
+    if (!r) {
+        writeError(err, "is not a live resource");
+        return nullptr;
+    }
+    if (type && std::strcmp(r->type, type) != 0) {
+        writeError(err, "is a " + std::string(r->type) + " resource, not a " + type);
+        return nullptr;
+    }
+    // get() refused an id with no owner left, so the pin below cannot fail; a table that disagrees is a host bug.
+    if (!self->resources_.pin(id)) {
+        writeError(err, "cannot be pinned");
+        return nullptr;
+    }
+    return r;
+}

+    ResourceHold() = default;
+    ResourceHold(const ResourceHold&) = delete;
+    ResourceHold& operator=(const ResourceHold&) = delete;
+    ResourceHold(ResourceHold&& other) noexcept

+    void drop() noexcept {
+        if (service && id) service->release(service->ctx, id);
+        service = nullptr;
+        id = 0;
+        resource = nullptr;
+    }
````

````diff
+RpcPutResourceResult EngineRpcService::putResource(BackendResourceSpec spec) {
+    RpcPutResourceResult out{std::nullopt, std::nullopt};
+    // A node reads a resource as one of three things (a system's ROM, its battery, a savestate), so the wire takes
+    // no other type: a resource of a type no node wants could only be a mistake in the caller.
+    if (spec.type != "rom" && spec.type != "sram" && spec.type != "state") {

+    }

+    if (sources != 1) {

+        if (bytes.empty()) {
+            out.error = "could not read " + *spec.path + ": the file is absent, unreadable or empty";
+            return out;
+        }
+    } else {

+            out.error = "\"" + *spec.embedded + "\" is not an embedded ROM";
+            return out;
+        }
+        bytes.assign(rom.begin(), rom.end());
+    }
+    // An empty byte block is a legitimate seed (a blank battery), but a ROM with no bytes has nothing to boot.
+    if (bytes.empty() && spec.type == "rom") {
+        out.error = "a rom resource cannot be empty: a zero-length ROM cannot boot";
+        return out;
+    }
+    std::string why;
+    const std::uint32_t id = engine_.putResource(spec.type, std::move(bytes), &why);
+    if (id == 0) {
+        out.error = why.empty() ? "the engine created no resource" : why;
+        return out;
+    }
+    out.id = id;
+    return out;
````

````bash
git commit -F - <<'EOF'
feat(engine): resources over RPC, and rp.host.resources/1 for a node that names one in its settings

putResource(spec) creates an immutable byte resource in the engine's
ResourceTable from bytes, a path native reads, or an embedded ROM's marker, and
answers its id or why not; releaseResource(id) is the owner's drop, idempotent.
Both join the emulator facet and run on the control thread like setGraph.
An empty byte block is a resource for a seed (a blank battery), but a rom
cannot be empty: a zero-length ROM would have nothing to boot.

A node that reads a resource its settings name says so with a field of type
rp::resource_ref<Type> ("res:N"). The authoring layer pins it at create through
rp.host.resources/1, which GraphHost answers over the engine's table, and drops
the pin when the instance is destroyed, so a resource a node holds is pinned for
the instance's life and the audio thread never takes or drops one. A field whose
ref moved is a rebuild, decided by node.hpp itself as well as by the type's
rebuild_key, and a missing, dropped or wrong-typed resource fails the create
with the field's name in the reason, and with it the document.

Planner-bound resource inputs cannot serve here: a port view exists only inside
a block, so a node cannot read a bound resource in activate, which is where a
system node builds its core in the next commit.
EOF
````

### Task 2: a system node builds its core at activation

Design section 5. The old path keeps working beside the new one: a node naming `core` still takes the core `buildCore`
parked, and a node naming `system` and a `rom` resource now builds its own. Every system node type (`rp.sameboy.gb`,
`rp.mesen.nes`, `rp.mesen.gba`, `rp.mesen.sms`) gains `system`, the three resource refs, an optional `romName` and its
construct-time fields (NES `sdRoot`, `fifo`, `fifoDepth`, `fifoBytesPerSecond`, `n8Link`, `n8LinkRttUs`,
`channelExportMode`; SMS `enableFm`, `gameGear`, which gets its own settings struct instead of sharing the GBA's). The
build goes through a new host interface, `rp.host.systems/1` (`build`, `destroy`), over the engine's one
`SystemFactory` and the typed configs the backends now take; the slot is claimed after the build and the plan's
`SystemTable` entry is filled as the node activates. The node seeds what the build applied, so its first application
restarts nothing.

````diff
+namespace {
+
+// A stereo document placing one system node that builds its own core: sys-<id> names `system` and its ROM resource,
+// with whatever construct-time settings or params the case adds.
+std::string builtDoc(SystemId id, const char* type, std::uint32_t rom, const std::string& extra = "",
+                     const std::string& params = "") {
+    const std::string node = "sys-" + std::to_string(id);
+    const std::string settings = R"({"system":)" + std::to_string(id) + R"(,"rom":"res:)" + std::to_string(rom) + "\"" +
+                                 (extra.empty() ? "" : "," + extra) + "}";
+    return R"({"nodes":[{"id":")" + node + R"(","type":")" + type + R"(","settings":)" + settings +
+           (params.empty() ? "" : R"(,"params":)" + params) +
+           R"(},{"id":"out","type":"rp.host.audio-out","settings":{"buses":[2]}}],
+                "wires":[{"from":")" + node + R"(.mix","to":"out.out.1-2"}]})";
+}
+
+Engine::GraphRequest builtRequest(std::string document, std::vector<SystemId> slots) {
+    return rp::host::test::graphRequest(std::move(document), std::move(slots));
+}
+
+// A document naming one system node that takes a parked core, with whatever settings the case adds beside it.
+std::string coreDoc(SystemId id, const char* type, const std::string& extra = "") {
+    const std::string node = "sys-" + std::to_string(id);
+    return R"({"nodes":[{"id":")" + node + R"(","type":")" + type + R"(","settings":{"core":)" +
+           std::to_string(id) + (extra.empty() ? "" : "," + extra) +
+           R"(}},{"id":"out","type":"rp.host.audio-out","settings":{"buses":[2]}}],
+                "wires":[{"from":")" + node + R"(.mix","to":"out.out.1-2"}]})";
+}
+
+// The one reason a refusal gives, as "node: code: message".
+std::string refusal(const Engine::GraphResult& r) {
+    if (r.ok || r.errors.size() != 1) return r.ok ? "ok" : std::to_string(r.errors.size()) + " errors";
+    const auto& e = r.errors.front();
+    return e.nodeId + ": " + e.code + ": " + e.message;
+}
+
+// A core that publishes nothing: claiming a snapshot slot for one costs no boot, so 64 of them can fill the pool.
+class EmptyCore final : public SystemBase {
+public:
+    explicit EmptyCore(SystemId id) : SystemBase(id) {}
+    SystemKind kind() const override { return SystemKind::SameBoy; }
+    void onActivate(double) override {}

+};

+}

+TEST_CASE("a plan refused for a busy ring destroys the core its node built", "[engine-graph][b2][systems]") {
+    Engine e(kRate);
+    const std::uint32_t rom = e.putResource("rom", readFile(RP_MGB_ROM_PATH));
+    REQUIRE(rom != 0);
+    const std::size_t cores = e.liveSystemCount(), slots = e.registry().liveCount();
+    // The test thread is the audio thread from here: a push only queues, so the ring fills and the plan's swap finds
+    // no room after its node built and claimed its core.
+    e.setAudioThreadOwns(true);
+    DspCommand bpm;
+    bpm.kind = DspCommand::Kind::SetBpm;
+    bpm.setBpm = {120.0};
+    while (e.pushCommand(bpm)) {
+    }
+    const auto refused = e.setGraph(builtRequest(builtDoc(1, rp::host::test::kGbType, rom), {1}));
+    CHECK_FALSE(refused.ok);
+    REQUIRE(refused.errors.size() == 1);
+    CHECK(refused.errors[0].code == "busy");
+    CHECK_FALSE(e.coreLive(1));
+    CHECK(e.liveSystemCount() == cores);
+    CHECK(e.registry().liveCount() == slots);
+    CHECK(e.resourcePinCount(rom) == 0);
+
+    // With the ring drained, the same document builds and keeps its core.
+    e.drainCommands();
+    REQUIRE(e.setGraph(builtRequest(builtDoc(1, rp::host::test::kGbType, rom), {1})).ok);
+    e.drainCommands();
+    CHECK(e.coreLive(1));
+    e.setAudioThreadOwns(false);
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("a document changing only a param or a live knob keeps a system node's core",
+          "[engine-graph][b2][systems]") {
+    Engine e(kRate);
+    const std::uint32_t rom = e.putResource("rom", readFile(RP_MGB_ROM_PATH));
+    REQUIRE(rom != 0);
+    const char* gb = rp::host::test::kGbType;
+    REQUIRE(e.setGraph(builtRequest(builtDoc(1, gb, rom), {1})).ok);
+    auto* core = e.findSystem(1);
+    REQUIRE(core != nullptr);
+    CHECK(e.liveSystemCount() == 1);
+
+    // Only the params: the store republishes the document for every edit, and the node's rebuild_key is unchanged, so the
+    // instance is reused and its core never rebuilds (a rebuild under the same id would refuse "system 1 is live").
+    CHECK(e.setGraph(builtRequest(builtDoc(1, gb, rom, "", R"({"gain":-6})"), {1})).ok);
+    CHECK(e.findSystem(1) == core);
+    CHECK(e.liveSystemCount() == 1);
+
+    // Only a live knob: applied to the same core at its next block.
+    CHECK(e.setGraph(builtRequest(builtDoc(1, gb, rom, R"("highpass":"off")"), {1})).ok);
+    CHECK(e.findSystem(1) == core);
+    CHECK(e.liveSystemCount() == 1);
+
+    // The identical document again: nothing changed, nothing built.
+    CHECK(e.setGraph(builtRequest(builtDoc(1, gb, rom, R"("highpass":"off")"), {1})).ok);
+    CHECK(e.findSystem(1) == core);
+    CHECK(e.liveSystemCount() == 1);
+    CHECK(e.resourcePinCount(rom) == 1);
+
+    // A document mixing the two paths: the pre-fill puts the parked core in sys-2's slot, and sys-1's node keeps the
+    // core it built.
+    auto parked = mgb(2);
+    auto* parkedRaw = parked.get();
+    REQUIRE(e.parkCore(std::move(parked)));
+    const std::string mixed =
+        R"({"nodes":[{"id":"sys-1","type":"rp.sameboy.gb","settings":{"system":1,"rom":"res:)" +
+        std::to_string(rom) + R"("}},{"id":"sys-2","type":"rp.sameboy.gb","settings":{"core":2}},
+            {"id":"out","type":"rp.host.audio-out","settings":{"buses":[2,2]}}],
+            "wires":[{"from":"sys-1.mix","to":"out.out.1-2"},{"from":"sys-2.mix","to":"out.out.3-4"}]})";
+    const auto mix = e.setGraph(builtRequest(mixed, {1, 2}));
+    CHECK(mix.ok);
+    CHECK(e.findSystem(1) == core);
+    CHECK(e.findSystem(2) == parkedRaw);
+    CHECK(e.liveSystemCount() == 2);
+    CHECK(e.registry().liveCount() == 2);
+    CHECK(e.resourcePinCount(rom) == 1);
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("a build outside the setGraph that activates it is refused rather than joining the live cores",
+          "[engine-graph][b2][systems]") {
+    Engine e(kRate);
+    const std::uint32_t rom = e.putResource("rom", readFile(RP_MGB_ROM_PATH));
+    REQUIRE(rom != 0);
+    SystemBuildRequest request;
+    request.rom = readFile(RP_MGB_ROM_PATH);
+    request.config = SameBoyConfig{};
+    std::string why;
+    CHECK(e.buildSystem(1, request, &why) == nullptr);
+    CHECK(why.find("setGraph") != std::string::npos);
+    CHECK_FALSE(e.coreLive(1));
+    CHECK(e.liveSystemCount() == 0);
+    CHECK(e.registry().liveCount() == 0);
+    CHECK(e.resourcePinCount(rom) == 0);
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("a core node's romName and construct-time fields are not build inputs, so changing one keeps its core",
+          "[engine-graph][b2][systems]") {
+    // A `core` node takes a core already built from buildCore's spec, so a field only a builder reads changes nothing on
+    // it. Carrying one in rebuild_key would rebuild on the next document that dropped it, and the fresh instance would
+    // find no parked core to take.
+    SECTION("a Game Boy's romName") {
+        Engine e(kRate);
+        REQUIRE(e.parkCore(mgb(1)));
+        REQUIRE(e.setGraph(builtRequest(coreDoc(1, rp::host::test::kGbType, R"("romName":"mGB")"), {1})).ok);
+        auto* core = e.findSystem(1);
+        REQUIRE(core != nullptr);
+        const auto dropped = e.setGraph(builtRequest(coreDoc(1, rp::host::test::kGbType), {1}));
+        CHECK(dropped.ok);
+        CHECK(e.findSystem(1) == core);
+        CHECK(e.liveSystemCount() == 1);
+        CHECK(e.registry().liveCount() == 1);
+    }
+    SECTION("a NES construct-time field") {
+        Engine e(kRate);
+        REQUIRE(e.parkCore(bliptoaster(1)));
+        REQUIRE(e.setGraph(builtRequest(coreDoc(1, rp::host::test::kNesType, R"("channelExportMode":"pinsPlusRef")"), {1})).ok);
+        auto* core = e.findSystem(1);
+        REQUIRE(core != nullptr);
+        const auto dropped = e.setGraph(builtRequest(coreDoc(1, rp::host::test::kNesType), {1}));
+        CHECK(dropped.ok);
+        CHECK(e.findSystem(1) == core);
+    }
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("a system built from resources joins and leaves while an audio thread runs its blocks",
+          "[engine-graph][b2][systems][sanitizer]") {
+    Engine e(kRate);
+    const std::uint32_t rom = e.putResource("rom", readFile(RP_MGB_ROM_PATH));
+    REQUIRE(rom != 0);
+    e.setAudioThreadOwns(true);
+    std::atomic<bool> running{true};
+    std::atomic<int>  blocks{0};
+    std::thread       audio([&] {
+        std::vector<std::vector<float>> lanes(2, std::vector<float>(512, 0.0f));
+        float* outs[2] = {lanes[0].data(), lanes[1].data()};
+        while (running.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) {
+            e.drainCommands();
+            e.processBlock(512, outs, 2);
+            blocks.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_release);
+        }
+    });
+    auto waitBlocks = [&](int n) {
+        const int seen = blocks.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
+        while (blocks.load(std::memory_order_acquire) < seen + n) std::this_thread::yield();
+    };
+    for (SystemId id = 1; id <= 3; ++id) {
+        REQUIRE(e.setGraph(builtRequest(builtDoc(id, rp::host::test::kGbType, rom), {id})).ok);
+        // The plan the audio thread adopts is the block thread's view, so the control thread watches the live cores
+        // instead: the build put this one there before the plan was published.
+        CHECK(e.coreLive(id));
+        waitBlocks(2);
+        REQUIRE(e.setGraph(builtRequest(rp::host::test::stereoDocument({}), {})).ok);
+        // The audio thread hands the old plan back on its next block; the core leaves with it.
+        const auto deadline = std::chrono::steady_clock::now() + std::chrono::seconds(10);
+        while (e.coreLive(id) && std::chrono::steady_clock::now() < deadline) {
+            e.reclaim();
+            std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(1));
+        }
+        CHECK_FALSE(e.coreLive(id));
+        waitBlocks(2);
+    }
+    running.store(false, std::memory_order_release);
+    audio.join();
+    e.setAudioThreadOwns(false);
+    e.reclaim();
+    CHECK(e.liveSystemCount() == 0);
+    CHECK(e.registry().liveCount() == 0);
+    CHECK(e.resourcePinCount(rom) == 0);
+}

+// ---- a node that builds its own core (docs/modular-graph-phase-c3-design.md sections 3 and 5) ---------------------
+
+namespace {
+
+// A `system` node's settings: the id it builds, its ROM resource, and whatever else the case adds.
+std::string buildSettings(SystemId system, std::uint32_t rom, const std::string& extra = "") {
+    return R"({"system":)" + std::to_string(system) + R"(,"rom":"res:)" + std::to_string(rom) + "\"" +
+           (extra.empty() ? "" : "," + extra) + "}";
+}
+
+// The resource id a byte block goes in as.
+std::uint32_t resource(NodeRig& rig, const char* type, std::vector<std::uint8_t> bytes) {
+    return rig.put(type, std::move(bytes));
+}
+
+// The bytes of a fixture the resources tree holds, or empty when it is not there (as CI runs): the LSDj and GBA ROMs
+// are not in the repository.
+std::vector<std::uint8_t> resourceFixture(const char* relative) {
+    const char* root = std::getenv("RETROPLUG_RESOURCES_DIR");
+    if (!root) return {};
+    return readFile((std::string(root) + relative).c_str());
+}
+
+// Run `core` directly for `blocks` blocks of 512 frames, as the engine's triad would, and return the savestate it then
+// has: the seed a later core restores, as a duplicate's or a saved state's.
+std::vector<std::uint8_t> stateAfter(SystemBase& core, int blocks) {
+    Direct d({&core}, 2, {{0, 1}});
+    for (int b = 0; b < blocks; ++b) d.block(512);
+    return core.saveStateBytes();
+}

+TEST_CASE("a Game Boy node built from its ROM resource renders what a core built from the same bytes renders",
+          "[engine-graph][system-node][resources]") {
+    const auto rom = readFile(RP_MGB_ROM_PATH);
+    SECTION("no seed") {
+        NodeRig rig(kRate);
+        auto direct = mgb(1);
+        const auto romId = resource(rig, "rom", rom);
+        REQUIRE(rig.set(R"({"nodes":[{"id":"sys-1","type":"rp.sameboy.gb","settings":)" +
+                        buildSettings(1, romId, R"("model":"dmgB","fastBoot":false)") +
+                        R"(},{"id":"out","type":"rp.host.audio-out","settings":{"buses":[2]}}],
+                            "wires":[{"from":"sys-1.mix","to":"out.out.1-2"}]})").ok);
+        Direct d({direct.get()}, 2, {{0, 1}});
+        CHECK(compare(rig, d, 2.0) == "");
+        CHECK(sounds(d));
+    }
+    SECTION("an sram seed") {
+        NodeRig rig(kRate);
+        SameBoyConfig cfg;
+        cfg.model = SameBoyModel::DmgB;
+        cfg.fastBoot = false;
+        cfg.sram.assign(8 * 1024, 0x5a);
+        auto direct = std::make_unique<SameBoySystem>(1, cfg, rom);
+        direct->onActivate(kRate);
+        const auto romId = resource(rig, "rom", rom);
+        const auto sramId = resource(rig, "sram", cfg.sram);
+        REQUIRE(rig.set(R"({"nodes":[{"id":"sys-1","type":"rp.sameboy.gb","settings":)" +
+                        buildSettings(1, romId, R"("model":"dmgB","fastBoot":false,"sram":"res:)" + std::to_string(sramId) + "\"") +
+                        R"(},{"id":"out","type":"rp.host.audio-out","settings":{"buses":[2]}}],
+                            "wires":[{"from":"sys-1.mix","to":"out.out.1-2"}]})").ok);
+        Direct d({direct.get()}, 2, {{0, 1}});
+        CHECK(compare(rig, d, 2.0) == "");
+        CHECK(sounds(d));
+    }
+    SECTION("a state seed") {
+        NodeRig rig(kRate);
+        auto source = mgb(9);
+        const auto state = stateAfter(*source, 24);
+        REQUIRE(!state.empty());
+        SameBoyConfig cfg;
+        cfg.model = SameBoyModel::DmgB;
+        cfg.fastBoot = false;
+        cfg.savestate = state;
+        auto direct = std::make_unique<SameBoySystem>(1, cfg, rom);
+        direct->onActivate(kRate);
+        const auto romId = resource(rig, "rom", rom);
+        const auto stateId = resource(rig, "state", state);
+        REQUIRE(rig.set(R"({"nodes":[{"id":"sys-1","type":"rp.sameboy.gb","settings":)" +
+                        buildSettings(1, romId, R"("model":"dmgB","fastBoot":false,"state":"res:)" + std::to_string(stateId) + "\"") +
+                        R"(},{"id":"out","type":"rp.host.audio-out","settings":{"buses":[2]}}],
+                            "wires":[{"from":"sys-1.mix","to":"out.out.1-2"}]})").ok);
+        Direct d({direct.get()}, 2, {{0, 1}});
+        CHECK(compare(rig, d, 2.0) == "");
+    }
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("a non-default model reaches a Game Boy core before it boots, so a savestate seed is not lost to a restart",
+          "[engine-graph][system-node][resources]") {
+    // The state is taken from a core running as the model the document names: the node built at the default model and
+    // restarted into CGB would lose exactly this. SameBoy's own restart discards the savestate it just restored.
+    const auto rom = readFile(RP_MGB_ROM_PATH);
+    SameBoyConfig sourceCfg;
+    sourceCfg.model = SameBoyModel::Mgb;
+    sourceCfg.fastBoot = true;
+    auto source = std::make_unique<SameBoySystem>(9, sourceCfg, rom);
+    source->onActivate(kRate);
+    const auto state = stateAfter(*source, 400);  // past the boot chime, so the state carries signal
+    REQUIRE(!state.empty());
+
+    NodeRig rig(kRate);
+    SameBoyConfig cfg = sourceCfg;
+    cfg.savestate = state;
+    auto direct = std::make_unique<SameBoySystem>(1, cfg, rom);
+    direct->onActivate(kRate);
+    const auto romId = resource(rig, "rom", rom);
+    const auto stateId = resource(rig, "state", state);
+    REQUIRE(rig.set(R"({"nodes":[{"id":"sys-1","type":"rp.sameboy.gb","settings":)" +
+                    buildSettings(1, romId, R"("model":"mgb","state":"res:)" + std::to_string(stateId) + "\"") +
+                    R"(},{"id":"out","type":"rp.host.audio-out","settings":{"buses":[2]}}],
+                        "wires":[{"from":"sys-1.mix","to":"out.out.1-2"}]})").ok);
+    // The core the node built is the model the document carried; it never restarted into anything.
+    auto* built = dynamic_cast<SameBoySystem*>(rig.builtCore(1));
+    REQUIRE(built != nullptr);
+    CHECK(built->config_.model == SameBoyModel::Mgb);
+    Direct d({direct.get()}, 2, {{0, 1}});
+    // mGB itself is silent as an Mgb (its chime is a DMG boot ROM's), so the comparison is the observation: a core
+    // restarted into another model would not follow this state bit for bit.
+    CHECK(compare(rig, d, 2.0) == "");
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("a NES node built from its ROM resource takes its region, export mode and expansion volume",
+          "[engine-graph][system-node][resources]") {
+    const auto rom = readFile(RP_BLIPTOASTER_ROM_PATH);
+    NodeRig rig(kRate);
+    MesenNesConfig cfg;
+    cfg.romPath = RP_BLIPTOASTER_ROM_PATH;
+    cfg.region = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(NesRegion::Ntsc);
+    cfg.channelExportMode = 1;  // stereoModPins: three mono streams
+    cfg.expansionVolume = 50;   // the blob path builds the core AT the volume; the node gives its param at its first block
+    auto direct = std::make_unique<MesenNesSystem>(1, cfg, rom);
+    direct->onActivate(kRate);
+    const auto romId = resource(rig, "rom", rom);
+    REQUIRE(rig.set(R"({"nodes":[{"id":"sys-1","type":"rp.mesen.nes","settings":)" +
+                    buildSettings(1, romId, R"("region":"ntsc","channelExportMode":"stereoModPins")") +
+                    R"(,"params":{"expansionVolume":50}},{"id":"out","type":"rp.host.audio-out","settings":{"buses":[1,1,1]}}],
+                        "wires":[{"from":"sys-1.pins.pulse","to":"out.out.1"},{"from":"sys-1.pins.tnd","to":"out.out.2"},
+                                 {"from":"sys-1.pins.expansion","to":"out.out.3"}]})").ok);
+    auto* built = rig.builtCore(1);
+    REQUIRE(built != nullptr);
+    CHECK(dynamic_cast<MesenNesSystem*>(built)->config().region == static_cast<std::uint32_t>(NesRegion::Ntsc));
+    Direct d({direct.get()}, 3, {{0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2}});  // a mono stream's two lanes are one buffer
+    CHECK(compare(rig, d, 3.0, afterBoot(*direct, *built)) == "");
+    CHECK(sounds(d));
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("a Master System node built from its ROM resource boots with FM off", "[engine-graph][system-node][resources]") {
+    NodeRig rig(kRate);
+    auto direct = sms(1);
+    const auto romId = resource(rig, "rom", readFile(RP_SMS_ROM_PATH));
+    // smsggdj reads its options from the battery: the same image, and the same seed sms() builds the core with.
+    std::vector<std::uint8_t> sram(32 * 1024, 0);
+    const std::uint8_t header[] = {'S', 'M', 'D', 'J', '4', 1, 32}, options[] = {0x43, 0x46, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0};
+    std::memcpy(sram.data(), header, sizeof header);
+    std::memcpy(sram.data() + 0x3f60, options, sizeof options);
+    const auto sramId = resource(rig, "sram", sram);
+    REQUIRE(rig.set(R"({"nodes":[{"id":"sys-1","type":"rp.mesen.sms","settings":)" +
+                    buildSettings(1, romId, R"("sram":"res:)" + std::to_string(sramId) + R"(","enableFm":false,
+                        "romName":"smsggdj_v0_45")") +
+                    R"(},{"id":"out","type":"rp.host.audio-out","settings":{"buses":[2]}}],
+                        "wires":[{"from":"sys-1.mix","to":"out.out.1-2"}]})").ok);
+    auto* built = rig.builtCore(1);
+    REQUIRE(built != nullptr);
+    CHECK_FALSE(dynamic_cast<MesenSmsSystem*>(built)->config().enableFm);
+    Direct d({direct.get()}, 2, {{0, 1}});
+    CHECK(compare(rig, d, 5.0, smsStart(*direct, *built)) == "");
+    CHECK(sounds(d));
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("a GBA node built from its ROM resource renders what a core built from the same bytes renders",
+          "[engine-graph][system-node][resources]") {
+    // The GBA is the one console whose typed path no other resource case reaches, and its ROM is a sibling fixture, so
+    // the case leaves on a run without one (as CI's) rather than failing there.
+    const auto rom = resourceFixture("/roms/nanoloop287d.gba");
+    if (rom.empty()) return;
+    NodeRig rig(kRate);
+    auto direct = std::make_unique<MesenGbaSystem>(1, MesenGbaConfig{}, rom);
+    direct->onActivate(kRate);
+    const auto romId = resource(rig, "rom", rom);
+    REQUIRE(rig.set(R"({"nodes":[{"id":"sys-1","type":"rp.mesen.gba","settings":)" + buildSettings(1, romId) +
+                    R"(},{"id":"out","type":"rp.host.audio-out","settings":{"buses":[2]}}],
+                        "wires":[{"from":"sys-1.mix","to":"out.out.1-2"}]})").ok);
+    auto* built = rig.builtCore(1);
+    REQUIRE(built != nullptr);
+    CHECK(dynamic_cast<MesenGbaSystem*>(built) != nullptr);
+    Direct d({direct.get()}, 2, {{0, 1}});
+    // Nanoloop plays nothing until it is told to: both cores get the same Start.
+    const auto start = [a = direct.get(), b = built, pressed = false](std::uint64_t at) mutable {
+        if (pressed || at < static_cast<std::uint64_t>(1.0 * kRate)) return;
+        for (SystemBase* s : {static_cast<SystemBase*>(a), b})
+            s->pressButton(static_cast<std::uint8_t>(GbaButton::Start), true);
+        pressed = true;
+    };
+    CHECK(compare(rig, d, 4.0, start) == "");
+    CHECK(d.sounded);
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("an LSDj node built from its ROM resource renders what a core built from the same bytes renders",
+          "[engine-graph][system-node][resources]") {
+    // A 1 MiB Game Boy ROM whose banking exercises more of the typed SameBoy path than the embedded mGB image does. The
+    // ROM is a sibling fixture, so the case leaves on a run without one (as CI's).
+    const auto rom = resourceFixture("/roms/lsdj/lsdj9_4_1-develop.gb");
+    if (rom.empty()) return;
+    NodeRig rig(kRate);
+    auto direct = std::make_unique<SameBoySystem>(1, SameBoyConfig{}, rom);
+    direct->onActivate(kRate);
+    const auto romId = resource(rig, "rom", rom);
+    REQUIRE(rig.set(R"({"nodes":[{"id":"sys-1","type":"rp.sameboy.gb","settings":)" + buildSettings(1, romId) +
+                    R"(},{"id":"out","type":"rp.host.audio-out","settings":{"buses":[2]}}],
+                        "wires":[{"from":"sys-1.mix","to":"out.out.1-2"}]})").ok);
+    auto* built = rig.builtCore(1);
+    REQUIRE(built != nullptr);
+    CHECK(dynamic_cast<SameBoySystem*>(built) != nullptr);
+    Direct d({direct.get()}, 2, {{0, 1}});
+    CHECK(compare(rig, d, 2.0) == "");
+    CHECK(d.sounded);
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("a Master System node without a romName stages each system under a stem of its own",
+          "[engine-graph][system-node][resources]") {
+    NodeRig rig(kRate);
+    const auto romId = resource(rig, "rom", readFile(RP_SMS_ROM_PATH));
+    const std::string document =
+        R"({"nodes":[{"id":"sys-1","type":"rp.mesen.sms","settings":)" + buildSettings(1, romId, R"("enableFm":false)") +
+        R"(},{"id":"sys-2","type":"rp.mesen.sms","settings":)" +
+        buildSettings(2, romId, R"("enableFm":false,"romName":"smsggdj_v0_45")") +
+        R"(},{"id":"out","type":"rp.host.audio-out","settings":{"buses":[2,2]}}],
+            "wires":[{"from":"sys-1.mix","to":"out.out.1-2"},{"from":"sys-2.mix","to":"out.out.3-4"}]})";
+    REQUIRE(rig.set(document).ok);
+    auto* unnamed = dynamic_cast<MesenSmsSystem*>(rig.builtCore(1));
+    auto* named = dynamic_cast<MesenSmsSystem*>(rig.builtCore(2));
+    REQUIRE(unnamed != nullptr);
+    REQUIRE(named != nullptr);
+    // Mesen reads the battery's stem out of the staged file's name, so two systems staged under one fallback name share
+    // one battery. A node with no romName gets its system id in the stem; a node with one stages under that instead.
+    const std::filesystem::path staged(unnamed->stagedRomPath()), explicitName(named->stagedRomPath());
+    CHECK(staged.stem().string() == "system-1");
+    CHECK(explicitName.stem().string() == "smsggdj_v0_45");
+    CHECK(staged != explicitName);
+}
+
+// ---- what a boot costs (docs/modular-graph-phase-c3-design.md section 9) --------------------------------------------
+
+TEST_CASE("a boot's cost per console, through the build a system node makes", "[.][bench]") {
+    using Clock = std::chrono::steady_clock;
+    auto micros = [](Clock::time_point t0) { return std::chrono::duration<double, std::micro>(Clock::now() - t0).count(); };
+    constexpr int kRuns = 5;
+
+    NodeRig rig(kRate);
+    const auto embedded = rp::embeddedMgbRom();
+    struct Boot {
+        const char*               name;
+        SystemConfig              config;
+        std::vector<std::uint8_t> rom;
+    };
+    std::vector<Boot> boots;
+    boots.push_back({"mGB (embedded)", SameBoyConfig{}, {embedded.begin(), embedded.end()}});
+    if (auto lsdj = resourceFixture("/roms/lsdj/lsdj9_4_1-develop.gb"); !lsdj.empty())
+        boots.push_back({"LSDj", SameBoyConfig{}, std::move(lsdj)});
+    boots.push_back({"NES", MesenNesConfig{}, readFile(RP_BLIPTOASTER_ROM_PATH)});
+    boots.push_back({"Master System", MesenSmsConfig{}, readFile(RP_SMS_ROM_PATH)});
+    if (auto gba = resourceFixture("/roms/nanoloop287d.gba"); !gba.empty())
+        boots.push_back({"GBA", MesenGbaConfig{}, std::move(gba)});
+
+    std::printf("\nboot through rp.host.systems/1's build at %.1f kHz: construct, onActivate (ROM, battery, savestate), the "
+                "state snapshot, and the same build through setGraph (slot claim and one plan with it); median of %d runs\n",
+                kRate / 1000.0, kRuns);
+    for (auto& boot : boots) {
+        std::vector<double> built, planned;
+        for (int run = 0; run < kRuns; ++run) {
+            SystemBuildRequest request;
+            request.rom = boot.rom;
+            request.config = boot.config;
+            std::string why;
+            const auto t0 = Clock::now();
+            std::unique_ptr<SystemBase> core = rig.factory.build(1, request, kRate, &why);
+            built.push_back(micros(t0));
+            REQUIRE(core);
+        }
+        // The same boot where it happens in the engine: a plan with one system node, published on a quiescent engine.
+        Engine engine(kRate);
+        const std::string type = std::holds_alternative<SameBoyConfig>(boot.config)   ? "rp.sameboy.gb"
+                                 : std::holds_alternative<MesenNesConfig>(boot.config) ? "rp.mesen.nes"
+                                 : std::holds_alternative<MesenSmsConfig>(boot.config) ? "rp.mesen.sms"
+                                                                                       : "rp.mesen.gba";
+        for (int run = 0; run < kRuns; ++run) {
+            const std::uint32_t romId = engine.putResource("rom", boot.rom);
+            REQUIRE(romId != 0);
+            const auto t0 = Clock::now();
+            const auto placed = engine.setGraph(rp::host::test::graphRequest(
+                R"({"nodes":[{"id":"sys-1","type":")" + type + R"(","settings":{"system":1,"rom":"res:)" +
+                    std::to_string(romId) + R"("}},{"id":"out","type":"rp.host.audio-out","settings":{"buses":[2]}}],
+                        "wires":[{"from":"sys-1.mix","to":"out.out.1-2"}]})",
+                {1}));
+            planned.push_back(micros(t0));
+            REQUIRE(placed.ok);
+            REQUIRE(engine.setGraph(rp::host::test::graphRequest(rp::host::test::stereoDocument({}), {})).ok);
+            engine.reclaim();
+        }
+        std::sort(built.begin(), built.end());
+        std::sort(planned.begin(), planned.end());
+        std::printf("  %-16s boot %7.1f ms   through setGraph %7.1f ms   (%zu KiB of ROM)\n", boot.name,
+                    built[built.size() / 2] / 1000.0, planned[planned.size() / 2] / 1000.0, boot.rom.size() / 1024);
+    }
+}
````

- [ ] **Step 2: Run the tests to see them fail**

Run: `cmake --build build --target retroplug-engine-graph-test -j$(nproc)`
Expected: FAIL: the build stops at the names this task adds: `rp.host.systems/1`, `SystemConfig`, `SystemBuildRequest`, `MesenSmsConfig::romName`, `MesenSmsSystem::stagedRomPath`, and the SMS settings type.

- [ ] **Step 3: The host service, the plan's table, and the nodes' settings**

`HostServices.hpp` gains `HostSystems` and its interface name beside the old `HostCores`, which stays as it is;
`SystemTable.hpp` states its invariant (a pre-parked slot is filled here, a `system` node's is null until its
activation fills it, the table is complete before publication and nothing writes it after). `Engine::buildSystem`
refuses id 0, an id out of range, a live id and a build outside a `setGraph`, builds through the engine's own factory,
claims the snapshot slot (seeding it from the core, after the build), records the live core and fills the plan's table
entry; `Engine::destroySystem` releases the slot, leaves the map and deletes the core. `publishGraph` reads a node's
`system` or its `core`, refuses two nodes naming one system, and keeps the `core`-only checks. The four settings
structs carry the new fields, a shared `validate` refuses both paths, neither, and a `system` without a `rom`, each
type makes its typed config, and `activate` builds when `system != 0` else takes the parked core; after a build
`applied` is seeded from the settings, less the Game Boy's capture, which the typed config does not carry:

````diff
+SystemBase* Engine::buildSystem(std::uint64_t system, const SystemBuildRequest& request, std::string* why) {

+    if (system == 0) return refuse("0 is not a system id");

+    // Checked before the claim, for the reason parkCore checks it: the registry finds a slot by id, and a second slot
+    // under a live id would free the live core's. A node of a plan not yet reclaimed still holds its core, so a
+    // construct-time edit under the id it was built with is refused here rather than quietly sharing it.
+    if (coreLive(id)) return refuse("system " + std::to_string(id) + " is live");
+    std::unique_ptr<SystemBase> core = factory_->build(id, request, sampleRate_, why);

+    }
+    // The slot is claimed after the build, not before, because the claim seeds the slot from the core: a GBA pays its
+    // whole boot (its 8 MiB ROM included) before a full pool can refuse it. That is the price of one claim that both
+    // keeps the slot and seeds it, and only a document that finds the pool full pays it.
+    if (!registry_.claim(id, *core)) return refuse("the snapshot pool is full");

+    // core answered to, and the table is published with the plan once every node has activated.
+    if (building_) {

+                e.nes = dynamic_cast<MesenNesSystem*>(built);
+                found = true;
+            }
+        if (!found) std::fprintf(stderr, "[engine] system %u built outside the plan's slots\n", static_cast<unsigned>(id));
+    }

+}

+void Engine::destroySystem(SystemBase* core) {
+    if (!core) return;
+    const SystemId id = core->id();
+    registry_.release(id);
+    liveCores_.erase(id);
````

- [ ] **Step 4: The typed build in the backends**

`SystemFactory` gains `SystemConfig` (a variant of the four typed configs) and `SystemBuildRequest` (the ROM, the
seeds, `romName` and the config), and `buildTyped` picks the backend by the config alternative; the blob's path
decodes into the same structs, so both paths boot identically. SameBoy's ROM gate moves into the shared typed build;
Mesen's three per-console build functions are the one place that gates, constructs, activates and enables the
snapshot, with the blob path decoding into theirs. `MesenSmsConfig` gains `romName`, and an unnamed system stages
under `system-<id>` so two unnamed systems never share Mesen's battery identity:

````diff
diff --git a/packages/native/src/system/SystemFactory.cpp b/packages/native/src/system/SystemFactory.cpp
index 89eed439..0640a110 100644
--- a/packages/native/src/system/SystemFactory.cpp
+++ b/packages/native/src/system/SystemFactory.cpp
@@ -12,3 +12,16 @@ std::unique_ptr<SystemBase> SystemFactory::build(SystemId id, const SystemBuildS
     if (it == backends_.end()) return nullptr;  // unknown core
     return it->second->build(id, spec, sampleRate);
 }
+
+std::unique_ptr<SystemBase> SystemFactory::build(SystemId id, const SystemBuildRequest& request,
+                                                 double sampleRate, std::string* why) const {
+    // Which backend serves a request is the console its config names: one Mesen core builds three consoles, one
+    // SameBoy core builds the Game Boy.
+    const char* core = std::holds_alternative<SameBoyConfig>(request.config) ? "sameboy" : "mesen";
+    const auto it = backends_.find(core);
+    if (it == backends_.end()) {
+        if (why) *why = std::string("the host has no ") + core + " core";
+        return nullptr;
+    }
+    return it->second->buildTyped(id, request, sampleRate, why);
+}

+std::unique_ptr<SystemBase> MesenBackend::buildTyped(SystemId id, const SystemBuildRequest& request,
+                                                     double sampleRate, std::string* why) {
+    if (const auto* nes = std::get_if<MesenNesConfig>(&request.config)) {

+        cfg.savestate = request.savestate;

+        cfg.sram = request.sram;
+        cfg.savestate = request.savestate;
+        return buildGba(id, std::move(cfg), request.rom, sampleRate, why);
+    }
+    if (const auto* sms = std::get_if<MesenSmsConfig>(&request.config)) {
+        MesenSmsConfig cfg = *sms;
+        cfg.sram = request.sram;
+        cfg.savestate = request.savestate;
+        cfg.romName = request.romName;
+        return buildSms(id, std::move(cfg), request.rom, sampleRate, why);
+    }
````

````bash
git commit -F - <<'EOF'
feat(engine): a system node builds its core at activation from the ROM and seed resources its settings name, through rp.host.systems/1

A system node's settings now name the core it runs one of two ways: its
`system` and the `rom`, `sram` and `state` resources it is built from, or (the
path C2 had) the parked `core` it takes. A node that names both, or neither,
or a system without its ROM, is refused at create with a reason naming the two
paths. The construct-time fields are settings too (a NES's sdRoot, FIFO
profile and its two overrides, the N8 link and its round trip, its export mode;
a SMS's enableFm and Game Gear), labels and ranges as the role configs spell
them, and they are in rebuild_key: an edit builds the core rather than being
applied to a live one.

The build happens in activate, on the control thread, inside the setGraph that
publishes the node: rp.host.systems/1 hands the engine a typed request (the
console, the bytes, the ROM's name and the console's config, every knob in it)
and the engine builds it at the plan's rate, claims the snapshot slot under the
system id and records the live core. The backend applies what it applies before
onActivate, boots, restores the seeds and enables the state snapshot, so a
non-default model never restarts the core it just restored; the node's own
first application then finds every value equal and calls nothing, except the
knobs the config does not carry (the Game Boy's capture mode). The backends'
blob path (buildCore) decodes its role configs into the same structs and calls
the same per-console build function, so both paths boot through one piece of
code and the ROM gates stay.

A failure (the ROM gate, a core that refuses to boot, an id a live core still
holds, a full snapshot pool) throws its reason, which the planner reports as
activate-failed on the node; the running plan keeps running and what the
refused plan built is destroyed as it unwinds, its slot released. A built core
is destroyed at the reclaim that frees the node's plan, on the control thread,
and stage 1 releases the node's resources with it. A taken core still goes back
through rp.host.cores/1, which keeps working until C3's last commit.

publishGraph tells the two paths apart by which field a system node's settings
carry, and builds the plan's system table with the slots' ids: the old path's
cores are in it before planning, and a built one joins as its node activates,
so the table is complete before the plan is published.

The node's params still land at its first block, after the build: a NES built
at its config's default expansion volume gets the document's value before its
first step, which the twins hold to a core the blob builds at that volume
already, bit for bit.

Also updated: the two native descriptor readers that assumed a settings schema
has one $defs entry (it now has the resource refs' too), and the three test
input helpers that captured their cores by reference to a call's parameters.
EOF
````

### Task 3: the TS switch-over, its construct-time reset, and the goldens

Design sections 4 and 6. TS owns a system's resources: `graph/systemResources.ts` is the one helper (`ResourcePool`
counts handles per resource id, `sameSource` decides ROM reuse, `bootSystem` puts a ROM and its optional seeds and
answers the handles, `romNameOf` the staged stem), and every verb that called `buildCore` keeps its orchestration over
it: puts first, then the id, then one publish, and a release only once the replacing document has published. The store
entry carries its platform, its `romName` and its resources instead of its `built` facts; `buildGraph` writes `system`,
`rom`, `sram`, `state`, `romName` and the construct-time fields; `DirectGraph` and the mock backend follow. A
construct-time edit is the reset path, run by `setRoleConfig` itself, compared through the role schema's parse of the
stored config and carrying the battery. The store remembers which id a rebuild replaced, so a `reset` of the old id
resets the replacement and answers its new id: the pre-C3 `setRoleConfig` + `reset(id)` pattern keeps working, and
`sdk-types.d.ts` records both the new contract and that compatibility. The B1 and role goldens are re-recorded (NES
documents split, 238 -> 298, moving 714 case indices), and the new no-fixture test file gains its skip-baseline entry.

**Files:** 76 files, by step below.
- Create: `packages/retroplug/src/graph/systemResources.ts`, `packages/retroplug/test-native/app-construct-edit.test.ts`, `packages/retroplug/test/systems/store-resources.test.ts`
- Modify: 73 files
