````ts
// A system's resources, as the store owns them (docs/modular-graph-phase-c3-design.md section 6): a boot puts its ROM
// and its seeds, the document that follows names their ids, and the engine is told to drop one only after the document
// that stops naming it has planned. A refused document puts the store's model back, gives back what the edit put and
// reports the verb's failure; a project load drops the system a refusal names and publishes the rest. And a
// construct-time edit is a reset that carries the battery: a new id, the same ROM resource, a new value in the
// document.
import { test, expect } from "../../testing/harness";
import { MockBackend, sramBytesFor, stateBytesFor } from "../../testing/mockBackend";
import { SystemsStore } from "../../src/systemsStore";
import { ProjectStore } from "../../src/projectStore";
import { RecentStore } from "../../src/recentStore";
import { buildAppRegistry } from "../../src/appHost";
import { DirectGraph } from "../../src/graph/directGraph";
import type { ConstructSpec, SetGraphResult } from "../../src/backend";
import { warned } from "../_warnings";
import { canonicalJson } from "../../src/graph/canonicalJson";
import { gbRom, nesRom } from "./fixtures";

// A store with the real role registry: a system's core-config role is what carries a construct-time field.
function newStore() {
  const be = new MockBackend("/cfg");
  const store = new SystemsStore(be, () => {}, buildAppRegistry());
  return { be, store };
}

// The resource and graph calls in the order the store made them: what a boot put, when the document naming it went
// out, and when the resource it replaced was dropped.
const order = (be: MockBackend): string[] =>
  be.log.filter((e) => e === "putResource" || e === "releaseResource" || e === "setGraph");

// Refuse the next `n` documents with a reason naming `nodeId`, recording the request as the mock does.
function refuse(be: MockBackend, n: number, nodeId = "", code = "activate-failed"): void {
  const setGraph = be.setGraph.bind(be);
  be.setGraph = (request) => {
    if (n-- <= 0) return setGraph(request);
    be.graphRequests.push(request);
    const result: SetGraphResult = { ok: false, errors: [{ nodeId, port: "", code, message: "refused for the test" }] };
    return result;
  };
}

// `v` as a document carries it: canonical JSON, its keys sorted.
const canon = (v: unknown): unknown => JSON.parse(canonicalJson(v));

// The ids a boot put that the engine still holds, in put order (a refusals' id 0 aside).
const heldIds = (be: MockBackend): number[] =>
  be.putResourceCalls.map((c) => c.id).filter((id) => id > 0 && be.resource(id) !== undefined);

test("add: puts the ROM and the battery seed, then publishes the document that names them", () => {
  const { be, store } = newStore();
  be.seed("/roms/a.gb", gbRom());
  be.seed("/roms/a.sav", "battery");
  const id = store.addSystem("/roms/a.gb")!;
  expect(order(be)).toEqual(["putResource", "putResource", "setGraph"]);
  // The ROM is the file the engine reads itself; the battery is the .sav, also by path (TS never holds its bytes).
  expect(be.putResourceCalls.map((c) => c.spec)).toEqual([
    { type: "rom", path: "/roms/a.gb" },
    { type: "sram", path: "/roms/a.sav" },
  ]);
  expect(canon(be.bootOf(id)!.settings)).toEqual(canon({
    system: id,
    rom: "res:1",
    sram: "res:2",
    romName: "a",
    model: "cgbC",
    highpass: "accurate",
    fastBoot: true,
    colorCorrection: "disabled",
    dmgPalette: "grey",
    lightTemperature: 0,
    serialOutCapture: "off",
  }));
});

test("remove: drops the document first, then gives every resource of the system back", () => {
  const { be, store } = newStore();
  be.seed("/roms/a.gb", gbRom());
  be.seed("/roms/a.sav", "battery");
  const id = store.addSystem("/roms/a.gb")!;
  const held = store.systems()[0].resources;
  be.log.length = 0;
  expect(store.removeSystem(id)).toBe(true);
  expect(order(be)).toEqual(["setGraph", "releaseResource", "releaseResource"]);
  expect(be.releaseResourceCalls).toEqual([held.rom, held.sram]);
  expect(heldIds(be)).toEqual([]);
});

test("reset: the same ROM boots again from its resource, and only the new seed is put", () => {
  const { be, store } = newStore();
  be.seed("/roms/a.gb", gbRom());
  be.seed("/roms/a.sav", "battery");
  const id = store.addSystem("/roms/a.gb")!;
  const before = store.systems()[0].resources;
  be.log.length = 0;
  const next = store.reset(id)!;
  // The ROM resource is shared, not put again; the battery is a new seed (the live one), put before the document.
  expect(order(be)).toEqual(["putResource", "setGraph", "releaseResource"]);
  expect(store.systems()[0].resources.rom).toBe(before.rom);
  expect(be.bootOf(next)!.sramBytes).toEqual(sramBytesFor(id)); // the live battery, read back rather than re-read
  expect(be.releaseResourceCalls).toEqual([before.sram]); // the old seed, after the document that stopped naming it
  expect(be.resource(before.rom)).toBeTruthy(); // the ROM is still the running plan's
});

test("reload: re-reads the ROM from disk, so its resource is put again rather than shared", () => {
  const { be, store } = newStore();
  be.seed("/roms/a.gb", gbRom());
  const id = store.addSystem("/roms/a.gb")!;
  const before = store.systems()[0].resources;
  be.log.length = 0;
  const next = store.reloadSystem(id)!;
  // The ROM and the live battery as a seed; then the document; then the two handles the old system held.
  expect(order(be)).toEqual(["putResource", "putResource", "setGraph", "releaseResource"]);
  expect(store.systems()[0].resources.rom === before.rom).toBe(false);
  expect(be.releaseResourceCalls).toEqual([before.rom]); // the old system held no seed: no .sav on disk
  expect(be.bootOf(next)!.rom!.spec).toEqual({ type: "rom", path: "/roms/a.gb" });
});

test("duplicate: shares the source's ROM and seeds the clone from its live state", () => {
  const { be, store } = newStore();
  be.seed("/roms/a.gb", gbRom());
  const id = store.addSystem("/roms/a.gb")!;
  const src = store.systems()[0].resources;
  be.log.length = 0;
  const copy = store.duplicateSystem(id)!;
  expect(order(be)).toEqual(["putResource", "setGraph"]); // the state seed, then the document; no ROM put
  const clone = store.systems().find((e) => e.id === copy)!;
  expect(clone.resources.rom).toBe(src.rom); // one resource, two handles
  expect(be.bootOf(copy)!.stateBytes).toEqual(stateBytesFor(id)); // the source's published machine
  expect(be.bootOf(copy)!.state!.source).toBe("bytes");
  // Removing the source keeps the clone's ROM: its handle is the one that is left.
  store.removeSystem(id);
  expect(be.resource(src.rom)).toBeTruthy();
  store.removeSystem(copy);
  expect(be.resource(src.rom)).toBe(undefined);
});

test("every put is balanced by a release once every system is gone", () => {
  const { be, store } = newStore();
  be.seed("/roms/a.gb", gbRom());
  be.seed("/roms/a.sav", "battery");
  be.seed("/roms/b.nes", nesRom());
  const a = store.addSystem("/roms/a.gb")!;
  const b = store.addSystem("/roms/b.nes")!;
  store.duplicateSystem(a);
  store.reset(a);
  store.reloadSystem(b);
  expect(heldIds(be).length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  for (const e of store.systems()) store.removeSystem(e.id);
  expect(store.systems().length).toBe(0);
  expect(heldIds(be)).toEqual([]); // every resource the engine was given has been given back
});

test("a refused publish puts the model back, gives back what it put, and reports the verb's failure", () => {
  const { be, store } = newStore();
  be.seed("/roms/a.gb", gbRom());
  be.seed("/roms/a.sav", "battery");
  const id = store.addSystem("/roms/a.gb")!;
  const before = store.systems()[0];
  const heldBefore = heldIds(be);
  const requests = be.graphRequests.length;
  refuse(be, 1);
  const failure = warned(() => store.reset(id));
  expect(failure.result).toBe(null); // the reason a buildCore that answered null gave, as the verb's failure
  expect(store.systems()[0]).toEqual(before); // the list as it was: the same id, the same handles
  expect(heldIds(be)).toEqual(heldBefore); // the seed the refused edit put is gone
  // The restored model is published again, so the engine keeps running the plan it ran (and the next edit starts from
  // a graph that matches the store). The refused document and that one are the two requests.
  expect(be.graphRequests.length).toBe(requests + 2);
  expect(be.graphRequests[be.graphRequests.length - 1].slots).toEqual([id]);
  expect(failure.warnings.length).toBeGreaterThan(0); // the engine's reason, and the rollback, are said
});

test("a project load drops the system a refusal names, with a note, and publishes the rest", () => {
  const be = new MockBackend("/cfg");
  be.seed("/roms/a.gb", gbRom());
  be.seed("/roms/b.nes", nesRom());
  be.seed("/roms/c.gb", gbRom());
  const project = new ProjectStore(be, new RecentStore(be), buildAppRegistry());
  project.systems.addSystem("/roms/a.gb");
  project.systems.addSystem("/roms/b.nes");
  project.systems.addSystem("/roms/c.gb");
  const bytes = project.exportBytes()!;

  be.seed("/proj/p.rplg.zip", bytes);
  const setGraph = be.setGraph.bind(be);
  let bad = 0;
  be.setGraph = (request) => {
    // The engine refuses the second system the load places, as a core that would not build does.
    const second = request.slots[1];
    if (!bad && second !== undefined) {
      bad = second;
      be.graphRequests.push(request);
      return { ok: false, errors: [{ nodeId: `sys-${second}`, port: "", code: "activate-failed", message: "the ROM is not a NES ROM" }] };
    }
    return setGraph(request);
  };
  const { warnings, result } = warned(() => project.load("/proj/p.rplg.zip"));
  be.setGraph = setGraph;
  expect(result).toEqual({ kind: "loaded", systems: 2 });
  const placed = be.lastDocument()!.nodes.filter((n) => n.id.startsWith("sys-")).map((n) => n.id);
  expect(placed.length).toBe(2);
  expect(placed.includes(`sys-${bad}`)).toBe(false); // the refused system is gone, the other two run
  expect(warnings.some((w) => w.includes("the engine refused it, so the project loads without it"))).toBe(true);
  // The dropped system's resources went with it.
  expect(project.systems.systems().every((e) => be.resource(e.resources.rom) !== undefined)).toBe(true);
});

test("a construct-time edit resets the system with its battery: a new id, the same ROM, the new value in the document", () => {
  const { be, store } = newStore();
  be.seed("/roms/a.nes", nesRom());
  const id = store.addSystem("/roms/a.nes")!;
  const before = store.systems()[0].resources;
  be.log.length = 0;
  expect(store.setRoleConfig(id, "mesen", { fifo: "hardware", fifoDepth: 4096 })).toBe(true);
  const next = store.systems()[0].id;
  expect(next === id).toBe(false); // a construct-time field is read at the build, so the node is rebuilt
  expect(store.systems().length).toBe(1);
  expect(store.focused()).toBe(next);
  // The live battery is carried: the seed is the old core's, read back rather than the .sav on disk.
  expect(be.bootOf(next)!.sramBytes).toEqual(sramBytesFor(id));
  expect(store.systems()[0].resources.rom).toBe(before.rom); // the same ROM resource
  const settings = be.bootOf(next)!.settings;
  expect(settings.fifo).toBe("hardware");
  expect(settings.fifoDepth).toBe(4096);
  // Nothing of the old system's is dropped: the ROM is shared and it held no seed (no .sav on disk). The one put is
  // the carried battery, made before the document that names it.
  expect(order(be)).toEqual(["putResource", "setGraph"]);
  expect(be.releaseResourceCalls).toEqual([]);
  expect(be.resource(before.rom)).toBeTruthy();
});

test("reset of the id a construct-time edit replaced resets what it became, carrying that system's battery", () => {
  const { be, store } = newStore();
  be.seed("/roms/a.nes", nesRom());
  const id = store.addSystem("/roms/a.nes")!;
  expect(store.setRoleConfig(id, "mesen", { fifo: "hardware", fifoDepth: 4096 })).toBe(true);
  const rebuilt = store.systems()[0].id;
  expect(rebuilt === id).toBe(false);
  const replacement = store.systems()[0].resources;
  // The pre-C3 contract: follow the construct-time edit with a reset of the id the caller held.
  be.log.length = 0;
  const next = store.reset(id);
  expect(next === null).toBe(false);
  expect(next === rebuilt).toBe(false); // the reset builds a system of its own, under a new id
  expect(store.systems().map((e) => e.id)).toEqual([next as number]);
  expect(store.focused()).toBe(next);
  // What it reset is the system the edit built: the new value is still its node's, and the battery it boots with is
  // the replacement's live one, not the system the caller's id named before the edit.
  expect(be.bootOf(next as number)!.settings.fifo).toBe("hardware");
  expect(be.bootOf(next as number)!.settings.fifoDepth).toBe(4096);
  expect(be.bootOf(next as number)!.sramBytes).toEqual(sramBytesFor(rebuilt));
  // The replacement's own seed is the one the document stopped naming, so it goes after the document planned; its ROM
  // is still the running plan's.
  expect(order(be)).toEqual(["putResource", "setGraph", "releaseResource"]);
  expect(be.releaseResourceCalls).toEqual([replacement.sram]);
  expect(be.resource(replacement.rom)).toBeTruthy();
});

test("reset follows a chain of rebuilds: the first id resets the live end of it", () => {
  const { be, store } = newStore();
  be.seed("/roms/a.nes", nesRom());
  const first = store.addSystem("/roms/a.nes")!;
  expect(store.setRoleConfig(first, "mesen", { fifo: "hardware" })).toBe(true);
  const second = store.systems()[0].id;
  expect(store.setRoleConfig(second, "mesen", { fifoDepth: 4096 })).toBe(true);
  const third = store.systems()[0].id;
  expect(third === second).toBe(false);
  const next = store.reset(first);
  expect(next === null).toBe(false);
  expect(next === third).toBe(false);
  expect(store.systems().map((e) => e.id)).toEqual([next as number]);
  // Both edits are still what its node names, and the battery carried is the live end's.
  expect(be.bootOf(next as number)!.settings.fifo).toBe("hardware");
  expect(be.bootOf(next as number)!.settings.fifoDepth).toBe(4096);
  expect(be.bootOf(next as number)!.sramBytes).toEqual(sramBytesFor(third));
});

test("the replaced-id map is capped: a very old id stops resolving, the recent ones still do", () => {
  const { be, store } = newStore();
  be.seed("/roms/a.nes", nesRom());
  const first = store.addSystem("/roms/a.nes")!;
  // Every construct-time edit replaces the system, so a session that does this hundreds of times must not keep every
  // id that ever named it. The cap keeps the most recent ones, which is what code written against the old contract
  // holds: it reset the id it had just edited.
  for (let i = 0; i < 200; i++) {
    const id = store.systems()[0].id;
    expect(store.setRoleConfig(id, "mesen", { fifo: "hardware", fifoDepth: 1000 + i })).toBe(true);
  }
  expect(store.systems().length).toBe(1);
  expect(store.reset(first)).toBe(null); // evicted long ago
  const recent = store.reset(first + 190);
  expect(recent === null).toBe(false);
  expect(store.systems().map((e) => e.id)).toEqual([recent as number]);
  expect(be.bootOf(recent as number)!.settings.fifoDepth).toBe(1199); // the live system's own value
  store.removeSystem(recent as number);
  expect(store.reset(first + 190)).toBe(null); // its chain ended with it
});

test("reset of a replaced id whose live system was removed answers null", () => {
  const { be, store } = newStore();
  be.seed("/roms/a.nes", nesRom());
  const id = store.addSystem("/roms/a.nes")!;
  expect(store.setRoleConfig(id, "mesen", { fifo: "hardware" })).toBe(true);
  const rebuilt = store.systems()[0].id;
  expect(store.removeSystem(rebuilt)).toBe(true);
  expect(store.reset(id)).toBe(null);
  expect(store.reset(rebuilt)).toBe(null);
  expect(store.systems()).toEqual([]);
  expect(heldIds(be)).toEqual([]);
});

test("only reset follows a replaced id: removeSystem of one does nothing, as it always has", () => {
  const { be, store } = newStore();
  be.seed("/roms/a.nes", nesRom());
  const id = store.addSystem("/roms/a.nes")!;
  expect(store.setRoleConfig(id, "mesen", { fifo: "hardware" })).toBe(true);
  const rebuilt = store.systems()[0].id;
  be.log.length = 0;
  expect(store.removeSystem(id)).toBe(false);
  expect(store.systems().map((e) => e.id)).toEqual([rebuilt]);
  expect(order(be)).toEqual([]); // no document, no release: the replaced id names nothing the store holds
  expect(be.resource(store.systems()[0].resources.rom)).toBeTruthy();
});

test("a construct-time edit that moves nothing live-rebuilds nothing, and a live knob stays a document", () => {
  const { be, store } = newStore();
  be.seed("/roms/a.nes", nesRom());
  const id = store.addSystem("/roms/a.nes")!;
  const resources = store.systems()[0].resources;
  be.log.length = 0;
  expect(store.setRoleConfig(id, "mesen", { region: "pal" })).toBe(true); // a live setting: a document
  expect(order(be)).toEqual(["setGraph"]);
  expect(store.systems()[0].id).toBe(id);
  expect(store.systems()[0].resources).toEqual(resources);
});

test("a construct-time edit whose rebuild is refused leaves the system as it was", () => {
  const { be, store } = newStore();
  be.seed("/roms/a.nes", nesRom());
  const id = store.addSystem("/roms/a.nes")!;
  const before = store.systems()[0];
  const heldBefore = heldIds(be);
  refuse(be, 1);
  expect(warned(() => store.setRoleConfig(id, "mesen", { fifo: "hardware" })).result).toBe(false);
  expect(store.systems()[0]).toEqual(before);
  expect(store.systems()[0].roles[0].config.fifo).toBe("instant"); // the edit went with the refused rebuild
  expect(heldIds(be)).toEqual(heldBefore);
});

test("a refused setting edit leaves the role as it was", () => {
  const { be, store } = newStore();
  be.seed("/roms/a.gb", gbRom());
  const id = store.addSystem("/roms/a.gb")!;
  const before = store.systems()[0];
  const n = be.graphRequests.length;
  refuse(be, 1);
  expect(store.setRoleConfig(id, "sameboy", { highpass: "off" })).toBe(false); // a setting: its document was refused
  expect(store.systems()[0]).toEqual(before);
  // The restored model is sent again, so the document the engine runs is the one the store holds.
  expect(be.graphRequests.length).toBe(n + 2);
  expect(be.lastBoot()!.id).toBe(id);
});

test("a sparse stored core config leaves a live knob and a param live, not a rebuild", () => {
  const { be, store } = newStore();
  be.seed("/roms/a.nes", nesRom());
  // A project saved before the mesen role schema grew its construct-time fields: the stored config holds only what
  // it knew. The comparison must use the schema's normalised view on both sides, or every omitted default looks like
  // a construct-time move and a live knob restarts the cart.
  const id = store.adopt({
    romPath: "/roms/a.nes",
    core: "mesen",
    roles: [{ kind: "mesen", config: { region: "pal" } }],
  })!;
  const resources = store.systems()[0].resources;
  be.log.length = 0;
  expect(store.setRoleConfig(id, "mesen", { removeSpriteLimit: true })).toBe(true); // a live setting: a document
  expect(store.systems()[0].id).toBe(id);
  expect(store.systems()[0].resources).toEqual(resources);
  expect(order(be)).toEqual(["setGraph"]);
  expect(be.graphNode(`sys-${id}`)?.settings?.removeSpriteLimit).toBe(true);

  be.log.length = 0;
  expect(store.setRoleConfig(id, "mesen", { expansionVolume: 40 })).toBe(true); // a param: live, no document
  expect(store.systems()[0].id).toBe(id);
  expect(store.systems()[0].resources).toEqual(resources);
  expect(order(be)).toEqual([]);
  expect(
    be.paramCalls.some((c) => c.nodeId === `sys-${id}` && c.paramId === "expansionVolume" && c.value === 40),
  ).toBe(true);
  expect(be.releaseResourceCalls).toEqual([]);
});

test("clear publishes the empty document and then gives every system's resources back", () => {
  const { be, store } = newStore();
  be.seed("/roms/a.gb", gbRom());
  be.seed("/roms/b.nes", nesRom());
  store.addSystem("/roms/a.gb");
  store.addSystem("/roms/b.nes");
  be.log.length = 0;
  store.clear();
  expect(order(be)).toEqual(["setGraph", "releaseResource", "releaseResource"]);
  expect(store.systems()).toEqual([]);
  expect(heldIds(be)).toEqual([]);
});

test("clear warns when the empty document is refused and still releases what it held", () => {
  const { be, store } = newStore();
  be.seed("/roms/a.gb", gbRom());
  be.seed("/roms/b.nes", nesRom());
  store.addSystem("/roms/a.gb");
  store.addSystem("/roms/b.nes");
  refuse(be, 1);
  const { warnings } = warned(() => store.clear());
  expect(store.systems()).toEqual([]);
  expect(heldIds(be)).toEqual([]);
  expect(warnings.some((w) => w.includes("[systems] clear: the engine refused the empty document"))).toBe(true);
});

test("discard drops one system and its resources at once, publishing nothing", () => {
  const { be, store } = newStore();
  be.seed("/roms/a.gb", gbRom());
  be.seed("/roms/b.nes", nesRom());
  const a = store.addSystem("/roms/a.gb")!;
  const b = store.addSystem("/roms/b.nes")!;
  const doomed = store.systems().find((e) => e.id === a)!;
  be.log.length = 0;
  expect(store.discard(a)).toEqual(doomed);
  expect(order(be)).toEqual(["releaseResource"]);
  expect(be.releaseResourceCalls).toEqual([doomed.resources.rom]);
  expect(store.systems().map((e) => e.id)).toEqual([b]);
  expect(be.resource(doomed.resources.rom)).toBe(undefined);
  expect(store.discard(999)).toBe(undefined);
  expect(order(be)).toEqual(["releaseResource"]); // nothing to drop for an id it does not hold
});

test("a restore republish that is refused too is reported, with the model still the one before the edit", () => {
  const { be, store } = newStore();
  be.seed("/roms/a.gb", gbRom());
  const id = store.addSystem("/roms/a.gb")!;
  const before = store.systems()[0];
  const heldBefore = heldIds(be);
  refuse(be, 2); // the edit's document, then the restored model's
  const failure = warned(() => store.reset(id));
  expect(failure.result).toBe(null);
  expect(store.systems()[0]).toEqual(before);
  expect(heldIds(be)).toEqual(heldBefore);
  expect(failure.warnings.some((w) => w.includes("the restored model was refused too"))).toBe(true);
});

test("DirectGraph puts each system's resources and releases them after the document that stopped naming them", () => {
  const be = new MockBackend("/cfg");
  be.seed("/roms/a.gb", gbRom());
  be.seed("/roms/b.nes", nesRom());
  const g = new DirectGraph(be);
  const spec = (romPath: string, platform: "gb" | "nes", core: "sameboy" | "mesen"): ConstructSpec => ({
    romPath,
    platform,
    core,
    embeddedRom: "",
    savPath: null,
    statePath: null,
  });
  be.log.length = 0;
  expect(g.add(spec("/roms/a.gb", "gb", "sameboy"), 1)).toBe(true);
  const first = be.bootOf(1)!;
  expect(order(be)).toEqual(["putResource", "setGraph"]);
  be.log.length = 0;
  expect(g.replace(1, spec("/roms/b.nes", "nes", "mesen"), 2)).toBe(true);
  // The replacing system's ROM is put before the document, the old one released only after it planned.
  expect(order(be)).toEqual(["putResource", "setGraph", "releaseResource"]);
  expect(be.releaseResourceCalls).toEqual([first.rom!.id]);
  be.log.length = 0;
  expect(g.remove(2)).toBe(true);
  expect(order(be)).toEqual(["setGraph", "releaseResource"]);
  expect(heldIds(be)).toEqual([]);
});

test("DirectGraph gives back a refused change's resources and keeps the ones it still places", () => {
  const be = new MockBackend("/cfg");
  be.seed("/roms/a.gb", gbRom());
  be.seed("/roms/b.nes", nesRom());
  const g = new DirectGraph(be);
  const gb: ConstructSpec = {
    romPath: "/roms/a.gb",
    platform: "gb",
    core: "sameboy",
    embeddedRom: "",
    savPath: null,
    statePath: null,
  };
  const nes: ConstructSpec = {
    romPath: "/roms/b.nes",
    platform: "nes",
    core: "mesen",
    embeddedRom: "",
    savPath: null,
    statePath: null,
  };
  expect(g.add(gb, 1)).toBe(true);
  const heldBefore = heldIds(be);
  be.log.length = 0;
  refuse(be, 1);
  expect(g.add(nes, 2)).toBe(false);
  expect(g.ids()).toEqual([1]);
  expect(heldIds(be)).toEqual(heldBefore);
  // The refused document (which this test's refusal helper records without logging), the resource its boot put given
  // back, then the restored model.
  expect(order(be)).toEqual(["putResource", "releaseResource", "setGraph"]);
  expect(be.graphRequests[be.graphRequests.length - 1].slots).toEqual([1]);
});
````

Create `packages/retroplug/test-native/app-construct-edit.test.ts`:

````ts
// A construct-time edit lands with no manual Reset (docs/modular-graph-phase-c3-design.md section 2): those fields are
// read once, when a system's node builds its core, so SystemsStore.setRoleConfig rebuilds the system itself - a new id,
// the same ROM resource, the live battery carried - and the new value is in the document that replaces the old one.
// Each case watches a real core change behaviour, not just the document:
//
//  - a NES's FIFO profile is its RX queue's capacity, which the transport stats report (0 = unbounded);
//  - a NES's channel export mode decides how many streams its node produces, which the per-channel render returns;
//  - an SMS's FM switch decides whether the YM2413 is emulated at all, so an FM-instrument song goes silent.
// And what a rebuild CARRIES: a construct-time edit and a reset the battery, a duplicate the whole machine, a load-state
// the file it was given. A Game Boy has no construct-time field of its own (its model and the rest are applied live), so
// its rebuilds are the reset path itself.
//
// Run with: `pnpm test:native app-construct-edit`.
import { test, expect, skip } from "../testing/harness";
import { createRealBackend } from "../src/realBackend";
import type { Backend } from "../src/backend";
import { createAudioDriver, type AudioDriver } from "../src/audioDriver";
import { RecentStore } from "../src/recentStore";
import { ProjectStore } from "../src/projectStore";
import { buildAppRegistry } from "../src/appHost";
import {
  buildMetronomeBlock,
  buildConfigBlock,
  buildSmdj4Sav,
  BLOCK_LEN,
  WRAM_BASE,
  P_PHRASES,
  P_CHAINS,
  P_SONG,
  P_INSTR,
  STEPS_PER_PHRASE,
  CHAIN_ENTRIES,
  HIT_NOTE,
  SMS_ROWS_PER_BEAT,
  SMS_SYNC_OFF,
} from "./smsSyncSong";

declare const __REPO_RESOURCES_DIR__: string;
declare const __RESOURCES_DIR__: string;
const NES = __REPO_RESOURCES_DIR__ + "/roms/bliptoaster.nes";
const SMS = __REPO_RESOURCES_DIR__ + "/roms/smsggdj_v0_45.sms";
const LSDJ = __RESOURCES_DIR__ + "/roms/lsdj/lsdj9_4_2.gb";

const rms = (a: Float32Array): number => {
  let s = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < a.length; i++) s += a[i] * a[i];
  return a.length ? Math.sqrt(s / a.length) : 0;
};

function session(): { be: Backend; audio: AudioDriver; project: ProjectStore } {
  const be = createRealBackend();
  const project = new ProjectStore(be, new RecentStore(be), buildAppRegistry());
  // A rebuild flushes the battery it replaces to the cart's sibling .sav; these are measurements against the fixtures
  // on disk, so nothing here may write to one (the offline render's own setting, setBatteryFlush).
  project.systems.setBatteryFlush(false);
  return { be, audio: createAudioDriver(project.graph), project };
}

// An FM-instrument song for smsggdj (sms-fm.test.ts's): channel 0 unused, channel 1 on an FM instrument, with the
// cart's own FM option on so it writes $F2 = 1. Audible only while RetroPlug emulates the YM2413.
const TYPE_FM = 4;
const FM_PROG_OFFSET = 12;
function fmSong(): Uint8Array {
  const b = buildMetronomeBlock();
  b[P_INSTR + 1 * 16] = TYPE_FM;
  b[P_INSTR + 1 * 16 + FM_PROG_OFFSET] = 1;
  for (let step = 0; step < STEPS_PER_PHRASE; step += SMS_ROWS_PER_BEAT)
    b.set([HIT_NOTE, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00], P_PHRASES + (STEPS_PER_PHRASE + step) * 4);
  for (let i = 0; i < CHAIN_ENTRIES; i++) b.set([0x01, 0x00], P_CHAINS + CHAIN_ENTRIES * 2 + i * 2);
  for (let row = 0; row < 8; row++) b.set([0xff, 0x01, 0xff, 0xff], P_SONG + row * 4);
  return b;
}

test("a NES FIFO profile edit reaches the core with no Reset: its RX queue's capacity is the new one", () => {
  const { be, project } = session();
  if (!be.fileExists(NES)) skip(`no ROM at ${NES}`);
  const id = project.systems.addSystem(NES)!;
  expect(be.getCoreTransportStats(id).rxCapacity).toBe(0); // the default profile is unbounded

  expect(project.systems.setRoleConfig(id, "mesen", { fifo: "hardware" })).toBe(true);
  const rebuilt = project.systems.view()[0].id;
  expect(rebuilt === id).toBe(false); // a construct-time field: the node is rebuilt under a new id
  expect(be.getCoreTransportStats(rebuilt).rxCapacity).toBe(2048); // rp::FIFO_HW_DEPTH, with no Reset pressed

  // And the explicit depth override, again with no Reset.
  expect(project.systems.setRoleConfig(rebuilt, "mesen", { fifoDepth: 4096 })).toBe(true);
  const deeper = project.systems.view()[0].id;
  expect(be.getCoreTransportStats(deeper).rxCapacity).toBe(4096);
  project.systems.removeSystem(deeper);
});

test("the pre-C3 contract still holds: a construct-time edit then reset(old id) answers a live system", () => {
  const { be, audio, project } = session();
  if (!be.fileExists(NES)) skip(`no ROM at ${NES}`);
  const store = project.systems;
  const id = store.addSystem(NES)!;
  // BlipToaster's helper does exactly this: apply the construct-time knob, then reset the id it was holding, which is
  // how code written before the store rebuilt inside setRoleConfig learned the id of the system that carried it.
  expect(store.setRoleConfig(id, "mesen", { n8Link: "off" })).toBe(true);
  const rebuilt = store.view()[0].id;
  expect(rebuilt === id).toBe(false);
  const next = store.reset(id);
  expect(next === null).toBe(false);
  expect(next === rebuilt).toBe(false);
  expect(store.view().map((e) => e.id)).toEqual([next as number]);
  expect(store.view()[0].roles.find((r) => r.kind === "mesen")!.config.n8Link).toBe("off");
  // The answer is a system the engine is running: its state is published, and a raw MIDI note plays it.
  expect(be.readState(next as number) !== null).toBe(true);
  audio.renderAudio(1500); // the ROM's boot, under the settings the reset gave it
  audio.stageMidiIn([0x90, 48, 127]);
  audio.renderAudio(200);
  audio.stageMidiIn([0x90, 48, 127]);
  const level = rms(audio.renderAudio(1000));
  console.log(`[construct-edit] reset of a replaced id: rms ${level.toFixed(5)}`);
  expect(level > 0.001).toBeTruthy();
  store.removeSystem(next as number);
});

test("a NES channel export mode edit reaches the core with no Reset: its per-channel streams appear", () => {
  const { be, audio, project } = session();
  if (!be.fileExists(NES)) skip(`no ROM at ${NES}`);
  const id = project.systems.addSystem(NES)!;
  audio.renderAudio(500);
  expect(audio.renderAudioPerChannel(id, 100).length).toBe(1); // mix: one stereo stream

  expect(project.systems.setRoleConfig(id, "mesen", { channelExportMode: "individualMono" })).toBe(true);
  const rebuilt = project.systems.view()[0].id;
  expect(rebuilt === id).toBe(false);
  audio.renderAudio(500);
  // The five core channels as raw mono stems: the mode is what the node builds the core with, so the stems appear
  // without a Reset.
  expect(audio.renderAudioPerChannel(rebuilt, 100).length).toBe(5);
  project.systems.removeSystem(rebuilt);
});

test("an SMS FM edit reaches the core with no Reset: an FM song goes silent", () => {
  const { be, audio, project } = session();
  if (!be.fileExists(SMS)) skip(`no ROM at ${SMS}`);
  const block = fmSong();
  const sav = buildSmdj4Sav(block, buildConfigBlock(SMS_SYNC_OFF, 1)); // the cart's own FM option on
  const id = project.systems.adopt(
    { romPath: SMS, roles: [{ kind: "mesen", config: { enableFm: true } }, { kind: "sms-sync", config: { machine: "sms" } }] },
    { sramBytes: sav },
  )!;
  const play = (system: number): number => {
    audio.renderAudio(3000); // boot: splash, config_load (takes fm_on), song_new
    for (let i = 0; i < BLOCK_LEN; i++)
      if (!be.writeCpu(system, WRAM_BASE + i, block[i])) throw new Error(`writeCpu failed at +0x${i.toString(16)}`);
    audio.pressButton(system, 7, true); // PAUSE: leave edit mode for play
    audio.renderAudio(100);
    audio.pressButton(system, 7, false);
    audio.renderAudio(500);
    return rms(audio.renderAudio(2500));
  };
  const withFm = play(id);
  expect(withFm > 0.001).toBeTruthy(); // the YM2413 is emulated, so the FM instrument sounds

  const battery = new Uint8Array(be.readSram(id)!);
  expect(project.systems.setRoleConfig(id, "mesen", { enableFm: false })).toBe(true);
  const rebuilt = project.systems.view()[0].id;
  expect(rebuilt === id).toBe(false);
  // The battery came across with the rebuild: the seed is the old core's SRAM, not the blank cartridge a cold boot
  // would give (this system was adopted from bytes, so there is no .sav on disk to re-read).
  expect(new Uint8Array(be.readSram(rebuilt)!)).toEqual(battery);
  const withoutFm = play(rebuilt);
  console.log(`[construct-edit] SMS FM song: enableFm true ${withFm.toFixed(5)}, after the edit ${withoutFm.toFixed(5)}`);
  expect(withoutFm < 0.001).toBeTruthy(); // no FM chip, so the song is silent - and no Reset was pressed
  project.systems.removeSystem(rebuilt);
});

test("duplicate takes the whole machine, reset carries the battery, load-state takes the file", () => {
  const { be, project } = session();
  if (!be.fileExists(LSDJ)) skip(`no ROM at ${LSDJ}`);
  const store = project.systems;
  const id = store.addSystem(LSDJ)!;
  // A distinguishing byte in the live battery, read back by every verb below: load a copy with its last byte flipped,
  // so a rebuild that cold-boots the cart (a blank battery) cannot pass the comparisons.
  const seeded = new Uint8Array(be.readSram(id)!);
  expect(seeded.length).toBeGreaterThan(0x8000);
  seeded[seeded.length - 1] ^= 0xff;
  const batteryPath = "/tmp/construct-edit-battery.sav";
  expect(be.writeFileAtomic(batteryPath, seeded)).toBe(true);
  const source = store.loadSram(id, batteryPath)!;
  const battery = new Uint8Array(be.readSram(source)!);
  expect(battery).toEqual(seeded);

  // Duplicate: the savestate, which carries work RAM as well as the battery.
  const dup = store.duplicateSystem(source)!;
  expect(new Uint8Array(be.readState(dup)!)).toEqual(new Uint8Array(be.readState(source)!));

  // Reset: the battery the core was running, not a cold one. (A Game Boy's config has no construct-time field - its
  // model and the rest are applied live - so this console's rebuilds are the reset path itself.)
  const reset = store.reset(source)!;
  expect(new Uint8Array(be.readSram(reset)!)).toEqual(battery);

  // Load state: the file's bytes, not the live machine.
  const statePath = "/tmp/construct-edit-state.ss0";
  const saved = new Uint8Array(be.readState(reset)!);
  expect(store.saveState(reset, statePath)).toBe(true);
  const loaded = store.loadState(reset, statePath)!;
  expect(loaded !== reset).toBe(true);
  expect(new Uint8Array(be.readState(loaded)!)).toEqual(saved);
  store.removeSystem(loaded);
  store.removeSystem(dup);
});

test("a project with one unreadable ROM loads the rest, with a note", () => {
  const { be } = session();
  if (!be.fileExists(NES)) skip(`no ROM at ${NES}`);
  // A ROM this build cannot boot: an iNES header with no PRG banks, which Mesen refuses. It classifies as NES, so a load
  // reaches the file and the engine's BUILD is what fails - the case a saved project has to survive, since a build that
  // fails answers null without refusing the project.
  const badPath = "/tmp/rp-construct-edit-bad.nes";
  const bad = new Uint8Array(16);
  bad.set([0x4e, 0x45, 0x53, 0x1a], 0); // "NES\x1A", 0 PRG banks, 0 CHR banks
  be.writeFileAtomic(badPath, bad);
  const projectPath = "/tmp/rp-construct-edit-bad.rplg";
  const systems = [
    { platform: "nes", core: "mesen", romPath: NES, roles: [{ kind: "mesen", config: {} }] },
    { platform: "nes", core: "mesen", romPath: badPath, roles: [{ kind: "mesen", config: {} }] },
    { platform: "gb", core: "sameboy", embeddedRom: "mgb", roles: [{ kind: "sameboy", config: {} }, { kind: "mgb", config: {} }] },
  ];
  be.writeFileAtomic(projectPath, new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify({ schemaVersion: "4", settings: {}, systems })));

  const fresh = new ProjectStore(be, new RecentStore(be), buildAppRegistry());
  fresh.systems.setBatteryFlush(false);
  const notes: string[] = [];
  const warn = console.warn;
  console.warn = (...args: unknown[]): void => void notes.push(args.map(String).join(" "));
  let outcome: unknown;
  try {
    outcome = fresh.load(projectPath);
  } finally {
    console.warn = warn;
  }
  console.log(`[construct-edit] a load with one unreadable ROM: ${JSON.stringify(outcome)}; notes: ${notes.join(" | ")}`);
  expect(outcome).toEqual({ kind: "loaded", systems: 2 }); // the two good systems, not the whole project lost
  expect(fresh.systems.systems().length).toBe(2);
  // Both are placed on the engine: a placed system's savestate snapshot answers a read.
  for (const e of fresh.systems.systems()) expect(be.readState(e.id) !== null).toBe(true);
  expect(notes.some((n: string) => n.includes("loads without it"))).toBe(true); // the note names what the load skipped
  be.deleteFile(badPath);
});
````

````diff
   expect(be.putResourceCalls.filter((c) => c.id === 0).length).toBe(4);
 });
 
+test("mock backend: a document naming a resource the engine does not hold is refused, as native refuses it", () => {
+  const be = new MockBackend("/cfg");
+  const rom = be.putResource({ type: "rom", bytes: Uint8Array.of(1, 2, 3) });
+  const sram = be.putResource({ type: "sram", bytes: Uint8Array.of(4) });
+  if ("error" in rom || "error" in sram) throw new Error("the puts should have been taken");
+  const doc = (settings: Record<string, unknown>): SetGraphRequest => ({
+    document: JSON.stringify({ nodes: [{ id: "sys-1", type: "rp.sameboy.gb", settings }], wires: [] }),
+    slots: [1],
+  });
+  const name = (field: string, id: number): Record<string, unknown> => ({ rom: `res:${rom.id}`, [field]: `res:${id}` });
+  expect(be.setGraph(doc(name("sram", sram.id))).ok).toBe(true); // a live rom and a live battery plan
+  // A dropped id is not a resource: the engine keeps its own table, and a stale reference must not name whatever took
+  // its place, so it is refused with the text native's node gives.
+  const dropped = be.putResource({ type: "sram", bytes: Uint8Array.of(9) });
+  if ("error" in dropped) throw new Error(dropped.error);
+  be.releaseResource(dropped.id);
+  expect(be.setGraph(doc(name("sram", dropped.id)))).toEqual({
+    ok: false,
+    errors: [{ nodeId: "sys-1", port: "", code: "create-failed", message: `sram: "res:${dropped.id}" is not a live resource` }],
+  });
+  expect(be.setGraph(doc(name("state", 999))).errors[0].message).toBe('state: "res:999" is not a live resource');
+  // A resource of another type, a field that is not a reference at all, and no ROM: each its own reason.
+  expect(be.setGraph(doc(name("sram", rom.id))).errors[0]).toEqual({
+    nodeId: "sys-1",
+    port: "",
+    code: "create-failed",
+    message: `sram: "res:${rom.id}" is a rom resource, not a sram`,
+  });
+  expect(be.setGraph(doc({ rom: "res:007" })).errors[0].message).toBe('rom: "res:007" is not a resource reference (res:N)');
+  expect(be.setGraph(doc({ sram: `res:${sram.id}` })).errors[0]).toEqual({
+    nodeId: "sys-1",
+    port: "",
+    code: "settings-invalid",
+    message: 'a system node names its ROM as {"rom": "res:N"}',
+  });
+});
+

@@ -1,5 +1,6 @@
-// The store classifies a ROM (platform.ts) and passes that platform + core to buildCore, so native
-// routes it to the right backend (sameboy / mesen-nes / mesen-gba). Embedded ROMs are always SameBoy.
+// The store classifies a ROM (platform.ts), and the platform picks the node type its core is placed as
+// (systemNodeTypeFor): the node's C++ type is what builds that console's core, so the platform and core the
+// entry carries and the node it is placed as are one decision. Embedded ROMs are always SameBoy.
 import { test, expect } from "../../testing/harness";
 import { MockBackend } from "../../testing/mockBackend";
 import { SystemsStore } from "../../src/systemsStore";
@@ -10,26 +11,27 @@ function makeStore() {
   return { be, store: new SystemsStore(be) };
 }
 
-test("buildCore carries the classified platform and core for each backend", () => {
-  const cases: Array<[string, Uint8Array, string, string]> = [
-    ["/roms/a.gb", gbRom(), "gb", "sameboy"],
-    ["/roms/a.nes", nesRom(), "nes", "mesen"],
-    ["/roms/a.gba", gbaRom(), "gba", "mesen"],
+test("a system's classified platform picks the node it is placed as, and the core its entry names", () => {
+  const cases: Array<[string, Uint8Array, string, string, string]> = [
+    ["/roms/a.gb", gbRom(), "rp.sameboy.gb", "gb", "sameboy"],
+    ["/roms/a.nes", nesRom(), "rp.mesen.nes", "nes", "mesen"],
+    ["/roms/a.gba", gbaRom(), "rp.mesen.gba", "gba", "mesen"],
   ];
-  for (const [path, bytes, platform, core] of cases) {
+  for (const [path, bytes, type, platform, core] of cases) {
     const { be, store } = makeStore();
     be.seed(path, bytes);
     expect(store.addSystem(path) != null).toBeTruthy();
-    const spec = be.buildCalls[be.buildCalls.length - 1];
-    expect(spec.platform).toBe(platform);
-    expect(spec.core).toBe(core);
+    expect(be.lastBoot()!.type).toBe(type);
+    expect(store.view()[0].platform).toBe(platform);
+    expect(store.view()[0].core).toBe(core);
   }
 });
 
-test("embedded mGB constructs as sameboy", () => {
+test("embedded mGB is placed as a Game Boy node, from its marker", () => {
   const { be, store } = makeStore();
   store.loadMgb();
-  const spec = be.buildCalls[be.buildCalls.length - 1];
-  expect(spec.platform).toBe("gb");
-  expect(spec.core).toBe("sameboy");

+  expect(spec.type).toBe("rp.sameboy.gb");
+  expect(spec.embeddedRom).toBe("mgb");
+  expect(spec.romName).toBe("mgb"); // the marker names the ROM: an embedded one has no path to take a stem from
 });
````

- [ ] **Step 3: The resource helper, and the store over it**

The helper and the platform table first, then the documents and the stores. `platform.ts` owns the one
`SystemNodeType` and derives it from the detected platform; `buildGraph` writes a system node's `system`, its resource
refs, `romName` (SMS/GG staged stem included), the construct-time fields beside C2's knobs, its params and, for a Game
Gear, `gameGear`; `systemKnobs` grows a `construct` column and `droppedKnobs` covers both tables. `systemsStore`
carries `platform`/`romName`/`resources` per entry, `commitEdit` publishes before it releases, `discard` drops a
refused load's resources at once, `reload` re-reads the ROM, and `setRoleConfig` runs a construct-time edit as a
rebuild under a new id with its battery, compared through its role schema's parsed view. `projectStore` drops the
system a refusal names and publishes the rest; `engineGraph` exposes the plan's errors; `DirectGraph` goes through the
helper; the mock backend refuses a document naming a dropped, unknown or wrong-typed resource, a bad `res:` spelling,
or a system node with no ROM. `settingsEnums` loses `roleConfigForNative`, the blob's encoder:

Create `packages/retroplug/src/graph/systemResources.ts`:

````ts
// One place that turns "what to boot" into what a system node names (docs/modular-graph-phase-c3-design.md
// section 6): the ROM and its two seeds as resources in the engine's table, and the ROM's name. The store and
// DirectGraph both boot a system this way, so a boot built for a store entry and one built for a literal
// DirectGraph spec are the same resources with the same settings. buildGraph writes the handles and the name
// into the node it places (graph/buildGraph.ts); a node never touches the filesystem.
//
// The seeds follow the core's own rule: seed bytes when TS holds them (an asset role's image, a battery read back from
// a live core, a project's blob), else the file by path when it is there, else NO seed - a missing `.sav` is a fresh
// cartridge, never a failure. A savestate wins over a battery, as it does at the core.
import type { ConstructSpec, EmulatorBackend, HostBackend, ResourceSpec, ResourceType } from "../backend";
import { systemNodeTypeFor, type SystemNodeType } from "../platform";
import { stem } from "../pathUtil";

/** The two resource calls a boot needs, plus the file check a seed by path is decided with. */
export type ResourceBackend = Pick<EmulatorBackend, "putResource" | "releaseResource"> &
  Pick<HostBackend, "fileExists">;

/** A node's settings name a resource as `"res:<id>"` (packages/native/src/graph/node.hpp): the resource's id in the
 *  engine's table, never a path. */
export const resourceRef = (id: number): string => `res:${id}`;

/** A system's resources, as the store counts and DirectGraph places them: the ROM its core boots from, and the seed
 *  its core starts with (the savestate, or the battery when it has no savestate). */
export interface SystemResources {
  rom: number;
  sram?: number;
  state?: number;
}

/** What a boot took and what a node is placed with: the node type its platform names, the resources, and the ROM's
 *  name (a Master System's staged file and battery identity, and an embedded ROM's marker). */
export interface BootedSystem {
  type: SystemNodeType;
  resources: SystemResources;
  romName: string;
  /** Every resource handle this boot holds, in the order it took them: a caller that gives the boot up hands these
   *  back, and a caller that keeps the system drops them when it goes. */
  handles: number[];
}

/** The handles a system's resources hold, in the order a boot took them (the ROM, the battery, the savestate): what a
 *  caller hands back when the system goes. */
export function systemHandles(resources: SystemResources): number[] {
  return [resources.rom, resources.sram, resources.state].filter((id): id is number => id !== undefined);
}

/** A boot that could not put its bytes: the reason the engine gave (an unreadable ROM, the failure the user saw when
 *  `buildCore` answered null), with every handle it had already taken given back. */
export type BootResult = BootedSystem | { error: string };

/** The ROM's name: the file's stem, or an embedded ROM's marker (`"mgb"`). Mesen stages a Master System or Game Gear
 *  ROM as a file and takes its battery stem from that name; every other console only needs a name that is its own. */
export function romNameOf(spec: Pick<ConstructSpec, "romPath" | "embeddedRom">): string {
  return spec.embeddedRom !== "" ? spec.embeddedRom : stem(spec.romPath);
}

/** The ROM a spec boots from: the bytes an asset role folded in (they already are the effective image), the marker of
 *  a ROM baked into the binary, or the file the engine reads itself (a GBA ROM can be 32 MB, and never crosses). */
function romSource(spec: ConstructSpec): ResourceSpec {
  if (spec.embeddedRom !== "") return { type: "rom", embedded: spec.embeddedRom };
  if (spec.romBytes && spec.romBytes.length > 0) return { type: "rom", bytes: spec.romBytes };
  return { type: "rom", path: spec.romPath };
}

/** A seed's source: the bytes when TS holds them, else the file by path when it is there, else none. */
function seedSource(
  type: ResourceType,
  bytes: Uint8Array | undefined,
  path: string | null,
  there: (p: string) => boolean,
): ResourceSpec | null {
  if (bytes) return { type, bytes };
  if (path && there(path)) return { type, path };
  return null;
}

/** The control plane's counted handles on the engine's resources: a resource is put once and named by every system
 *  that boots from it (an entry's ROM survives its rebuilds, and a duplicate shares its source's), and the engine is
 *  told to drop it when the last handle goes. The engine keeps a dropped resource readable while a plan still pins
 *  it, so a caller drops one only after the document that stops naming it has planned. */
export class ResourcePool {
  private counts = new Map<number, number>();
  private sources = new Map<number, ResourceSpec>();

  constructor(readonly backend: ResourceBackend) {}

  /** Put `spec` in the engine's table and take its first handle: the id, or the reason the engine refused it. */
  put(spec: ResourceSpec): { id: number } | { error: string } {
    const result = this.backend.putResource(spec);
    if ("error" in result) return { error: result.error };
    this.counts.set(result.id, (this.counts.get(result.id) ?? 0) + 1);
    this.sources.set(result.id, spec);
    return { id: result.id };
  }

  /** Whether the resource `id` was put from `spec`: true for the same file, the same embedded marker, or byte-for-byte
   *  the same image. A rebuild whose ROM bytes moved (an asset role folded a different image in) must not reuse the
   *  resource the old core read. */
  sameSource(id: number, spec: ResourceSpec): boolean {
    const was = this.sources.get(id);
    if (!was || was.type !== spec.type) return false;
    if ("path" in was && "path" in spec) return was.path === spec.path;
    if ("embedded" in was && "embedded" in spec) return was.embedded === spec.embedded;
    if (!("bytes" in was) || !("bytes" in spec) || was.bytes.length !== spec.bytes.length) return false;
    for (let i = 0; i < was.bytes.length; ++i) if (was.bytes[i] !== spec.bytes[i]) return false;
    return true;
  }

  /** Take another handle on a resource this pool holds, so a boot can share it: the same id. */
  retain(id: number): number {
    const held = this.counts.get(id) ?? 0;
    if (held === 0) throw new Error(`resource ${id} is not one this pool holds`);
    this.counts.set(id, held + 1);
    return id;
  }

  /** Give one handle back, telling the engine to drop the resource once it was the last. Absent ids are no-ops, so a
   *  caller can hand back the seeds a boot never took. */
  drop(id: number | undefined): void {
    if (id === undefined) return;
    const held = this.counts.get(id) ?? 0;
    if (held > 1) {
      this.counts.set(id, held - 1);
      return;
    }
    this.counts.delete(id);
    this.sources.delete(id);
    if (held === 1) this.backend.releaseResource(id);
  }

}

/** Boot `spec` from resources: put its ROM and its seeds, or answer why the engine refused one of them, having given
 *  back what it had already taken. `opts.rom` is a ROM resource to share when it was put from the same bytes (a rebuild
 *  of the same image, a duplicate of the same cart); a spec whose ROM moved puts its own. */
export function bootSystem(pool: ResourcePool, spec: ConstructSpec, opts: { rom?: number } = {}): BootResult {
  const handles: number[] = [];
  const giveBack = (error: string): BootResult => {
    for (const id of handles) pool.drop(id);
    return { error };
  };
  const source = romSource(spec);
  let rom: number;
  if (opts.rom !== undefined && pool.sameSource(opts.rom, source)) {
    rom = pool.retain(opts.rom);
  } else {
    const put = pool.put(source);
    if ("error" in put) return { error: put.error };
    rom = put.id;
  }
  handles.push(rom);
  let sram: number | undefined;
  let state: number | undefined;
  const there = (p: string): boolean => pool.backend.fileExists(p);
  // The battery first, then the savestate, as a core applies them (a savestate restored over its own battery is the
  // machine it was taken from).
  const sramPut = seedSource("sram", spec.sramBytes, spec.savPath, there);
  if (sramPut) {
    const put = pool.put(sramPut);
    if ("error" in put) return giveBack(put.error);
    sram = put.id;
    handles.push(sram);
  }
  const statePut = seedSource("state", spec.stateBytes, spec.statePath, there);
  if (statePut) {
    const put = pool.put(statePut);
    if ("error" in put) return giveBack(put.error);
    state = put.id;
    handles.push(state);
  }
  return { type: systemNodeTypeFor(spec.platform), resources: { rom, sram, state }, romName: romNameOf(spec), handles };
}
````

````diff
+    for (let next = this.replacedBy.get(cur); next !== undefined; next = this.replacedBy.get(cur)) cur = next;
+    return cur;
   }
+
+  /** Forget every chain that ends in `id`, which is about to stop being live: the ids that named it, and it. */
+  private forgetReplacementsEndingIn(id: number): void {
+    const dead: number[] = [];
+    for (const oldId of this.replacedBy.keys()) if (this.chainEnd(oldId) === id) dead.push(oldId);
+    for (const oldId of dead) this.replacedBy.delete(oldId);
+  }
+
+  // Boot `spec` and make the entry it becomes: the one place a store boot goes through, so every verb puts its
+  // resources the same way, takes the same handles and reports a put's refusal the same way. `rest` is the entry's
+  // identity and settings, everything but the ROM's name and the resources, which the boot answers.
+  private boot(
+    spec: ConstructSpec,
+    rest: Omit<SystemEntry, "romName" | "resources">,
+    opts: { rom?: number } = {},
+  ): Prepared | null {
+    const booted = bootSystem(this.pool, spec, opts);
+    if ("error" in booted) {
+      console.warn(`[systems] ${rest.romPath || `the embedded ${rest.embeddedRom}`}: ${booted.error}`);
+      return null;
+    }
+    return {
+      entry: { ...rest, romName: booted.romName, resources: booted.resources },
+      handles: booted.handles,
+    };
+  }
+
+  // Record an edit and publish the document that places it. A refused document puts the list and the focus back,
+  // gives back what the edit put, and sends the restored model again so the next edit starts from the graph that
+  // runs (EngineGraph keeps a refused document's systems as its model). The resources an edit REPLACES are released
+  // only once its document has planned: a dropped resource cannot be bound by a new instance, and a refused
+  // document's nodes are built afresh.
+  private commitEdit(
+    what: string,
+    edit: { entries: SystemEntry[]; focusedId?: number; put?: number[]; drop?: number[] },
+    rearmTap = true,
+  ): boolean {
+    const entries = this.entries;
+    const focusedId = this.focusedId;
+    this.entries = edit.entries;
+    if (edit.focusedId !== undefined) this.focusedId = edit.focusedId;
+    if (this.onGraphChange(rearmTap)) {
+      for (const id of edit.drop ?? []) this.pool.drop(id);
+      return true;
+    }
+    console.warn(`[systems] ${what}: the engine refused the document; the edit is rolled back`);
+    this.entries = entries;
+    this.focusedId = focusedId;
+    for (const id of edit.put ?? []) this.pool.drop(id);
+    if (!this.onGraphChange(rearmTap))
+      console.warn(`[systems] ${what}: the restored model was refused too; the engine keeps the previous plan`);
+    return false;
+  }
+}
+
+/** A system TS has booted, its resources put and its handles held, but not yet placed: the entry it becomes and the
+ *  handles its boot took, which an edit gives back when its document is refused. */
+interface Prepared {
+  entry: SystemEntry;
+  handles: number[];
 }
````

- [ ] **Step 4: Re-record the goldens**

The B1 golden file is rewritten by mapping each case's model through `buildGraph`, as its test's
header says; the role goldens are re-recorded by their own test. This plan's script does both checks (`rewrite` and
`compare`); it imports `buildGraph` from this worktree through the `@REPO@` its imports spell, which the command after
the block fills in from `$PWD`, so keep it in `/tmp/c3-resources`:

Save the script as `/tmp/c3-resources/c3-goldens.ts` (its imports spell this worktree as `@REPO@`):

````ts
// C3's golden tooling. `rewrite <build-graph.json>` re-records the B1 golden file's documents by mapping each case's
// model through buildGraph, the procedure build-graph-goldens.test.ts's header gives: each system gains the platform
// its node type names, its ROM resource (its own id) and that resource's name, and a NES the core config its export
// mode labels; every document is rebuilt and the documents deduplicated in first-seen order, so the cases' document
// indices are reassigned. `compare <old> <new>` holds every case of the new file to the old one by name: the same
// slots and tap, the same node ids, types and wires, and each system node the same but for the fields this adds.
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import {
  buildGraph,
  type GraphModel,
} from "@REPO@/packages/retroplug/src/graph/buildGraph";
import { canonicalJson } from
  "@REPO@/packages/retroplug/src/graph/canonicalJson";
import { CHANNEL_EXPORT_VALUES } from
  "@REPO@/packages/retroplug/src/settingsEnums";

type Node = { id: string; type: string; settings?: Record<string, unknown>; params?: Record<string, unknown> };
type Doc = { nodes: Node[]; wires: unknown[] };
type System = {
  id: number;
  type: string;
  exportMode?: number;
  platform?: string;
  romName?: string;
  resources?: { rom: number };
  coreConfig?: Record<string, unknown>;
};
type Case = { name: string; model: GraphModel; document: number; slots: number[]; tapArm: unknown };
type File = { documents: Doc[]; cases: Case[] };

const PLATFORMS: Record<string, string> = {
  "rp.sameboy.gb": "gb",
  "rp.mesen.nes": "nes",
  "rp.mesen.gba": "gba",
  "rp.mesen.sms": "sms",
};
const SYSTEM_TYPES = new Set(Object.keys(PLATFORMS));
const read = (path: string): File => JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, "utf8"));

function rewrite(path: string): void {
  const file = read(path);
  const documents: string[] = [];
  const index = new Map<string, number>();
  for (const c of file.cases) {
    for (const s of c.model.systems as unknown as System[]) {
      s.platform = PLATFORMS[s.type];
      s.resources = { rom: s.id };
      s.romName = `rom${s.id}`;
      // A NES's document carries the export mode its core config labels; with none there is no mode to label.
      if (s.type === "rp.mesen.nes") s.coreConfig = { channelExportMode: CHANNEL_EXPORT_VALUES[s.exportMode ?? 0] };
    }
    const built = buildGraph(c.model);
    const doc = canonicalJson(built.document);
    if (!index.has(doc)) {
      index.set(doc, documents.length);
      documents.push(doc);
    }
    c.document = index.get(doc) as number;
    c.slots = built.slots;
    c.tapArm = built.tapArm;
  }
  const cases = file.cases.map((c) => canonicalJson(c));
  writeFileSync(path, `{"documents":[\n${documents.join(",\n")}\n],"cases":[\n${cases.join(",\n")}\n]}\n`);
  console.log(`rewrote ${documents.length} documents of ${file.cases.length} cases in ${path}`);
}

function compare(oldPath: string, newPath: string): void {
  const before = read(oldPath);
  const after = read(newPath);
  const problems: string[] = [];
  let systemNodes = 0;
  let changedDocs = 0;
  let movedIndices = 0;
  // The fields C3 adds to a system node's settings and to a system's model: stripped from both sides before the
  // comparison, so what is left is what the case carried before, and anything that moved outside them is a problem.
  const STRIPPED = [
    "core", "system", "rom", "romName", "sram", "state", "sdRoot", "fifo", "fifoDepth", "fifoBytesPerSecond",
    "n8Link", "n8LinkRttUs", "channelExportMode", "enableFm", "gameGear",
  ];
  const ported = (settings: Record<string, unknown>) => {
    const out: Record<string, unknown> = {};
    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(settings)) if (!STRIPPED.includes(k)) out[k] = v;
    return out;
  };
  const stripModel = (m: GraphModel) => ({
    ...m,
    systems: m.systems.map((s) => {
      const { platform: _p, resources: _r, romName: _n, ...rest } = s as unknown as System;
      if (rest.coreConfig !== undefined) {
        const { channelExportMode: _c, ...core } = rest.coreConfig as Record<string, unknown>;
        if (Object.keys(core).length > 0) rest.coreConfig = core;
        else delete rest.coreConfig;
      }
      return rest;
    }),
  });
  const byName = (f: File, name: string) => f.cases.find((c) => c.name === name);
  const names = new Set([...before.cases.map((c) => c.name), ...after.cases.map((c) => c.name)]);
  for (const name of names) {
    const o = byName(before, name);
    const n = byName(after, name);
    if (!o || !n) {
      problems.push(`${name}: only in ${o ? "old" : "new"}`);
      continue;
    }
    if (canonicalJson(stripModel(o.model)) !== canonicalJson(stripModel(n.model))) {
      problems.push(`${name}: the model moved beyond the resource fields`);
    }
    if (canonicalJson(o.slots) !== canonicalJson(n.slots) || canonicalJson(o.tapArm) !== canonicalJson(n.tapArm)) {
      problems.push(`${name}: slots or tap moved`);
    }
    if (o.document !== n.document) movedIndices++;
    const od = before.documents[o.document];
    const nd = after.documents[n.document];
    if (canonicalJson(od.wires) !== canonicalJson(nd.wires)) problems.push(`${name}: wires moved`);
    if (od.nodes.length !== nd.nodes.length) {
      problems.push(`${name}: node count moved`);
      continue;
    }
    od.nodes.forEach((on, i) => {
      const nn = nd.nodes[i];
      if (on.id !== nn.id || on.type !== nn.type) {
        problems.push(`${name}: node ${i} is ${nn.id}, was ${on.id}`);
        return;
      }
      if (!SYSTEM_TYPES.has(on.type)) {
        if (canonicalJson(on) !== canonicalJson(nn)) problems.push(`${name}: ${on.id} (${on.type}) moved`);
        return;
      }
      systemNodes++;
      const core = on.settings?.core;
      const named = (field: string, want: unknown) => {
        const got = nn.settings?.[field];
        if (got !== want) problems.push(`${name}: ${on.id} names ${field} ${got}, was ${want}`);
      };
      named("system", core);
      named("rom", `res:${core}`);
      named("romName", `rom${core}`);
      if (canonicalJson(ported(on.settings ?? {})) !== canonicalJson(ported(nn.settings ?? {}))) {
        problems.push(`${name}: ${on.id}'s settings moved beyond the resource fields`);
      }
      if (canonicalJson(on.params) !== canonicalJson(nn.params)) problems.push(`${name}: ${on.id}'s params moved`);
      for (const k of Object.keys(nn)) {
        if (!["id", "type", "settings", "params"].includes(k)) problems.push(`${name}: ${on.id} gained ${k}`);
      }
    });
    if (canonicalJson(od) !== canonicalJson(nd)) changedDocs++;
  }
  console.log(
    `${newPath}: ${names.size} cases, ${changedDocs} with a changed document, ${movedIndices} whose document index ` +
      `moved, ${systemNodes} system nodes compared`,
  );
  if (problems.length) {
    console.log(`  PROBLEMS (${problems.length}):`);
    for (const p of problems.slice(0, 40)) console.log(`    ${p}`);
    process.exitCode = 1;
  } else {
    console.log("  nothing else moved: every other node, every wire, slot, tap and model field is as it was");
  }
}

const [mode, a, b] = process.argv.slice(2);
if (mode === "rewrite") rewrite(a);
else if (mode === "compare") compare(a, b);
else throw new Error("usage: rewrite <file> | compare <old> <new>");
````

Then fill in this worktree's path, so the script imports this tree's `buildGraph`, not another worktree's:

````bash
git commit -F - <<'EOF'
feat(graph): system nodes are placed from resources: the store puts each system's ROM and seeds, buildGraph names them, and a construct-time edit resets the system with its battery

A system node boots its own core from the resources its settings name (C3's
second commit, rp.host.systems/1), so the control plane moves onto that path:
one helper (graph/systemResources.ts) turns "what to boot" into the engine's
resources and the ROM's name, for the store and for DirectGraph alike, and
nothing in TS calls buildCore any more.

- ConstructSpec is TS's own description of a system to boot, not a wire type:
  it drops the opaque numeric settings blob, gains coreConfig (the role config
  in the labels a node reads), and only the resource helper reads it.
- SystemsStore counts handles on the resources per id: a rebuild that keeps
  the ROM shares it, a duplicate shares its source's, and a resource is
  released only after the document that stops naming it has planned. Every
  verb keeps its orchestration over the helper.
- A refused document puts the store's model back, gives back what the edit
  put, publishes the restored model again and reports the verb's failure; a
  project load drops the system a refusal names, with a note, and publishes
  the rest.
- A construct-time field's edit is a reset run by setRoleConfig itself: a new
  id, the same ROM resource, the live battery carried. The store remembers
  which id a rebuild replaced, so reset() of the old id - the pre-C3 SDK's
  pattern - still resets what it became and answers the live id.
- buildGraph writes system/rom/sram/state/romName, the construct-time fields
  (only valid values, noted at load like C2's dropped knobs) and C2's knobs.
- The mock refuses a document naming an unknown, dropped or wrong-typed
  resource in native's text; DirectGraph places systems through the helper.
- The goldens re-record: each case's model now carries its platform, resources
  and romName, a NES's coreConfig with the export-mode label its exportMode
  named, and a Game Gear's gameGear, so NES models that differed only by
  exportMode split 238 documents into 298 (714 cases moved index). The
  documents still differ only in their system nodes' settings, and the Catch2
  golden runner puts a resource per ROM they name and rewrites their refs.
EOF
````

### Task 4: the old path deleted, its callers moved

Design sections 3 ("What goes") and 5. The old path goes: `buildCore` and its facts, `BackendConstructSpec`,
`toBuildSpec`, `RpcBuiltCore`, the parked cores (`parkCore`, `takeCore`, the re-park a refused document's unwind did,
the free sweep and the re-rating), `rp.host.cores/1`, `SystemBuildSpec` and its blob with `decodeSameBoyRoleConfig` and
Mesen's two decoders, the RPC service's second `SystemFactory`, `SameBoyConfig::linkGroupId`, and the system nodes'
`core` field with its both/neither rule and its `unknown-core` / `core-type` refusals. Every caller that parked a core
moves to a resource-built document: `GraphDocs.hpp` puts one ROM per console per engine and rewrites a document's
`res:` ids in one pass, `NodeRig` boots through it, and each test that read a parked core reads the node's core
instead. `ConstructSpec` stays, as TS's own description of a boot. The sanitizer tags and the suites' counts
below are the report's.

````diff
-// The engine's side of graphs TS builds (docs/modular-graph-phase-b2-design.md section 2.5): a built core parks

-// published document placed is freed; a system node's settings carry its core's knobs beside the core
-// (docs/modular-graph-phase-c2-design.md section 4); and Engine::setParam reaches a param of the running plan at the

-// quiescent Engine, so every plan applies as it is published, except where a test owns the drain itself.

+// re-arm rides the swap, a refused document leaves the running plan as it was, and a system node builds its core from
+// the ROM resource its settings name and gives it back at reclaim; a system node's settings carry its core's knobs
+// beside the system it names (docs/modular-graph-phase-c2-design.md section 4); and Engine::setParam reaches a param of

+inline std::vector<std::uint8_t> readFile(const char* path) {
+    std::vector<std::uint8_t> bytes;
+    if (std::FILE* f = std::fopen(path, "rb")) {
+        std::fseek(f, 0, SEEK_END);
+        bytes.resize(static_cast<std::size_t>(std::ftell(f)));
+        std::fseek(f, 0, SEEK_SET);
+        if (std::fread(bytes.data(), 1, bytes.size(), f) != bytes.size()) bytes.clear();
+        std::fclose(f);
+    }
+    return bytes;
+}
+
+// A system a test document places (docs/modular-graph-phase-c3-design.md section 3): its id, the node type whose core
+// it builds, the `rom` resource that core is built from, and any further settings or params its case adds.
 struct DocSystem {
-    SystemId    id;
-    const char* type;  // rp.sameboy.gb / rp.mesen.nes / ...
+    SystemId      id;
+    const char*   type;  // rp.sameboy.gb / rp.mesen.nes / ...
+    std::uint32_t rom = 0;    // the id Engine::putResource gave its ROM (withRoms); 0 names none
+    std::string   extra;      // further settings members, JSON, without braces: a knob or a construct-time field
+    std::string   params;     // the node's param values, JSON members without braces
 };
 
 inline const char* const kGbType = "rp.sameboy.gb";
 inline const char* const kNesType = "rp.mesen.nes";
 
+// The ROM bytes a system node of `type` boots in a native test: the same fixture every case used, small enough to put
+// per Engine. A GBA node gates the bytes it is given (detectRomFormat), so its 1 KiB ROM - the smallest
+// GbaConsole::LoadRom takes - carries the Nintendo logo the way every licensed cart does. Empty for a type with no
+// fixture.
+inline std::vector<std::uint8_t> romFor(const std::string& type) {
+    if (type == kGbType) return readFile(RP_MGB_ROM_PATH);
+    if (type == kNesType) return readFile(RP_BLIPTOASTER_ROM_PATH);
+    if (type == "rp.mesen.sms") return readFile(RP_SMS_ROM_PATH);
+    if (type == "rp.mesen.gba") {
+        static constexpr std::uint8_t kGbaLogo[] = {
+            0x24, 0xFF, 0xAE, 0x51, 0x69, 0x9A, 0xA2, 0x21, 0x3D, 0x84, 0x82, 0x0A, 0x84, 0xE4, 0x09, 0xAD,
+            0x11, 0x24, 0x8B, 0x98, 0xC0, 0x81, 0x7F, 0x21, 0xA3, 0x52, 0xBE, 0x19, 0x93, 0x09, 0xCE, 0x20,
+        };
+        std::vector<std::uint8_t> rom(1024, 0);
+        std::copy(std::begin(kGbaLogo), std::end(kGbaLogo), rom.begin() + 0x04);
+        return rom;
+    }
+    return {};
+}
+
+// The `rom` resource a node of `type` builds from: its fixture put in `engine` now. 0, with the reason in *why, for a
+// type with no fixture or a put the engine refused.
+inline std::uint32_t putRom(Engine& engine, const std::string& type, std::string* why = nullptr) {
+    const auto rom = romFor(type);
+    if (rom.empty()) {
+        if (why) *why = "no ROM fixture for " + type;
+        return 0;
+    }
+    const std::uint32_t id = engine.putResource("rom", rom, why);
+    if (id == 0 && why && why->empty()) *why = "the engine would not take " + type + "'s ROM";
+    return id;
+}
+
+// `systems`, each naming the `rom` resource its node type boots: one put per console, so two systems of one console
+// share the bytes. A system that already names one (a test that put its own, a wrong-console ROM among them) keeps it.
+// Throws with the reason when a fixture is missing or refused, as NodeRig::put does.
+inline void withRoms(Engine& engine, std::vector<DocSystem>& systems) {
+    std::map<std::string, std::uint32_t> byType;
+    for (DocSystem& s : systems) {
+        if (s.rom != 0) continue;
+        const auto cached = byType.find(s.type);
+        if (cached != byType.end()) {
+            s.rom = cached->second;
+            continue;
+        }
+        std::string why;
+        const std::uint32_t rom = putRom(engine, s.type, &why);
+        if (rom == 0) throw std::runtime_error(why);
+        byType.emplace(s.type, rom);
+        s.rom = rom;
+    }
+}
+
+// `document` with every `"res:<id>"` replaced by the id `ids` gives it, in ONE pass: two ids can each be the other's
+// engine id, and replacing them one after another would let the second see the first's output. A document built by the
+// helpers below already names the engine's own ids; this is for documents spelled before an Engine had them (the
+// goldens' models). nullopt with the reason when the document names an id `ids` does not have.
+inline std::optional<std::string> rebindResources(const std::string& document,
+                                                  const std::map<std::uint32_t, std::uint32_t>& ids) {
+    std::string out;
+    for (std::size_t at = 0; at < document.size();) {
+        const auto found = document.find("\"res:", at);
+        if (found == std::string::npos) {
+            out.append(document, at, std::string::npos);
+            break;
+        }
+        out.append(document, at, found - at);
+        const auto digits = found + 5;  // past `"res:`
+        const auto end = document.find('"', digits);
+        if (end == std::string::npos) return std::nullopt;  // a reference runs off the document
+        const auto mapped = ids.find(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(std::stoul(document.substr(digits, end - digits))));
+        if (mapped == ids.end())
+            return "the document names " + document.substr(found, end - found + 1) + ", which no system of the model has";
+        out += "\"res:" + std::to_string(mapped->second) + "\"";
+        at = end + 1;
+    }
+    return out;
+}

+// smsggdj reads its options from the battery at boot: an empty SMDJ4 image with the v1 block ('C' 'F', then PAL / SYNC /
+// video / FM off, then their sum) at $3F60 of a 32 KB image, SYNC off so the song free-runs (smsSyncSong.ts).
+std::vector<std::uint8_t> smsBattery() {
+    std::vector<std::uint8_t> sram(32 * 1024, 0);
+    const std::uint8_t header[] = {'S', 'M', 'D', 'J', '4', 1, 32}, options[] = {0x43, 0x46, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0};
+    std::memcpy(sram.data(), header, sizeof header);
+    std::memcpy(sram.data() + 0x3f60, options, sizeof options);
+    return sram;
+}

+TEST_CASE("a system node placed at a gain plays its first block at it, from the first sample",
+          "[engine-graph][system-node][params]") {
+    // The core's gain smoother starts at unity, so applyGain snaps a node's first value: a node placed at -12 dB never
+    // plays a block at 0 dB. A node always builds its core fresh, so the block its gain first lands in is normally
+    // silent; a `state` seed taken while the DMG boot chime sounds makes it audible, and a ramp down from unity would
+    // show in it.
+    const auto rom = readFile(RP_MGB_ROM_PATH);
+    SameBoyConfig sourceCfg;
+    sourceCfg.model = SameBoyModel::DmgB;
+    sourceCfg.fastBoot = false;
+    auto source = std::make_unique<SameBoySystem>(9, sourceCfg, rom);
+    source->onActivate(kRate);
+    Direct run({source.get()}, 2, {{0, 1}});
+    // The seed is taken at a block boundary whose next 64 frames sound: the chime is a sequence of notes, so a
+    // boundary inside a note is what makes the node's first block audible.
+    std::vector<std::uint8_t> before = source->saveStateBytes(), state;
+    for (int b = 0; b < 4000 && state.empty(); ++b) {
+        run.sounded = false;
+        run.block(64);
+        if (run.sounded) state = before;
+        else before = source->saveStateBytes();
+    }
+    REQUIRE(!state.empty());
+
+    NodeRig rig(kRate);
+    SameBoyConfig cfg = sourceCfg;
+    cfg.savestate = state;
+    auto direct = std::make_unique<SameBoySystem>(1, cfg, rom);
+    direct->onActivate(kRate);
+    direct->setGainDb(-12.0f, true);  // the snap the node makes at its first block
+    const auto romId = resource(rig, "rom", rom);
+    const auto stateId = resource(rig, "state", state);
+    REQUIRE(rig.set(R"({"nodes":[{"id":"sys-1","type":"rp.sameboy.gb","settings":{)" +
+                    rig.boot("rp.sameboy.gb", 1,
+                             R"("model":"dmgB","fastBoot":false,"state":"res:)" + std::to_string(stateId) + "\"",
+                             romId) +
+                    R"(},"params":{"gain":-12}},{"id":"out","type":"rp.host.audio-out","settings":{"buses":[2]}}],
+                        "wires":[{"from":"sys-1.mix","to":"out.out.1-2"}]})").ok);
+    auto* const built = dynamic_cast<SameBoySystem*>(rig.builtCore(1));
+    REQUIRE(built != nullptr);
+    CHECK(built->config_.gainDb == 0.0f);  // the param lands at the first block, not at the build
+    // The seed's first block carries signal, which is what makes the snap observable there.
+    auto probe = std::make_unique<SameBoySystem>(1, cfg, rom);
+    probe->onActivate(kRate);
+    probe->setGainDb(-12.0f, true);
+    Direct first({probe.get()}, 2, {{0, 1}});
+    first.block(64);
+    REQUIRE(sounds(first));
+    // Bit for bit against a core snapped the same way: without the snap the node's first block sits at unity and ramps
+    // down, which the comparison covers inside its first 20 ms.
+    Direct d({direct.get()}, 2, {{0, 1}});
+    CHECK(compare(rig, d, 0.05) == "");
+    CHECK(sounds(d));
+    CHECK(built->config_.gainDb == -12.0f);
+}
````

- [ ] **Step 2: Delete the native old path**

The RPC's build method and wire DTOs, the parked cores and the plan's free sweep, the `core` half of the system nodes
(settings, keys, activate branch, destructor handoff, `SystemTarget`), the blob and its three decoders, the typed
build's only remaining caller path, `rp.host.cores/1`, and the second factory composition. `HostServices()` gets an
explicit default: deleting its copy constructor would otherwise suppress the implicit one:

````bash
git commit -F - <<'EOF'
refactor(engine): the old build path is gone: buildCore, the parked cores, the settings blob and its decoders, and the wire DTO

A system node builds its core at activation from the ROM and seed resources its settings name, so nothing
is built beside the graph any more: EngineRpcService::buildCore, toBuildSpec, the native mirror of TS's
default core and their BackendConstructSpec / RpcBuiltCore DTOs go, and rp.host.cores/1 (HostCores) with
its take/released handoff. Engine::parkCore, takeCore, the parked map, the re-park of a core a refused
document took, the free of what stayed parked and setSampleRate's parked half go too; HostServices keeps
one factory, the Engine's.

A system node names only its `system` and `rom`: the `core` setting, the activate branch that took a parked
core, the both/neither rule's core half and the unknown-core / core-type checks are gone, and a create that
names no system says so. SystemBuildSpec's opaque blob, SystemBackend's blob build, the blob paths in the
SameBoy and Mesen backends and the three *RoleConfig decoders go: one typed build function per console is
the only one.

TS loses EmulatorBackend.buildCore and BuiltCore, realBackend's specParams and buildCore, and the mock's
buildCore / buildCalls / mockSystem / buildable / nodeTypeFor / configNumber; ConstructSpec keeps its `core`
field, now documented as the role kind of its coreConfig, since nothing native reads it.

Every Catch2 test that parked a core now builds its system from resources: GraphDocs.hpp's DocSystem names
its `rom` resource and gains a shared one-pass rebind plus one put per console per Engine, NodeRig builds
through rp.host.systems/1, and each twin compares a node against a core built directly from the same bytes.

The blob's last config leftover goes with it: SameBoyConfig::linkGroupId, which only the deleted decoder wrote
and nothing read, so the cable is the plan's `link` wires throughout. Two cases pin what a fresh core could
otherwise hide: a node placed at a gain plays its first block at it (a savestate seed taken mid-chime, against
a directly snapped twin), and a reused node's core is in the new plan's table before any activation fills it.
The hosts' dead CoreBackends.hpp includes go, and the header says what is true: the Engine's one factory
registers the backends at its construction, and dispatch is by the typed config a request carries.
EOF
````

````diff
+once: the document it was in never planned, so nothing pinned them.
````
